liora-504ffa44e171.text: No. Stay with us, Zizzy. I'm not losing another one.

liora-c863c6edb1fc.speaker: liora
liora-c863c6edb1fc.text: No. Stay with us, Vexrath. I'm not losing another one.

liora-1bad726282d2.speaker: liora
liora-1bad726282d2.text: No. Stay with us, Nettle. I'm not losing another one.

liora-a654eb31950c.speaker: liora
liora-a654eb31950c.text: No. Stay with us, Ser Aldric. I'm not losing another one.

liora-c6219e27ac98.speaker: liora
liora-c6219e27ac98.text: Oh, Brambur. I'm so sorry. We carry you out, however long it takes.

liora-5fa7b3d16550.speaker: liora
liora-5fa7b3d16550.text: Oh, Fizzwick. I'm so sorry. We carry you out, however long it takes.

liora-ee35930d1237.speaker: liora
liora-ee35930d1237.text: Oh, Pip. I'm so sorry. We carry you out, however long it takes.

liora-65900282d4b3.speaker: liora
liora-65900282d4b3.text: Oh, Grumsh. I'm so sorry. We carry you out, however long it takes.

liora-f3bb7ad6f36c.speaker: liora
liora-f3bb7ad6f36c.text: Oh, Zizzy. I'm so sorry. We carry you out, however long it takes.

liora-492426118723.speaker: liora
liora-492426118723.text: Oh, Vexrath. I'm so sorry. We carry you out, however long it takes.

liora-fcc97473595e.speaker: liora
liora-fcc97473595e.text: Oh, Nettle. I'm so sorry. We carry you out, however long it takes.

liora-55e0e79d3efa.speaker: liora
liora-55e0e79d3efa.text: Oh, Ser Aldric. I'm so sorry. We carry you out, however long it takes.

malthrax-2580ca9c893f.speaker: malthrax
malthrax-2580ca9c893f.text: You think I came alone? WAKE, GORVAX!

narrator-32df22ce7ce0.speaker: narrator
narrator-32df22ce7ce0.text: Gorvax the Tyrant falls! The Blackspire's lights go dark.

narrator-782d7a6d41b4.speaker: narrator
narrator-782d7a6d41b4.text: The Blackspire is dark. Princess Elowen is home, and Emberhollow is free. Arise, Knight of the Dawn.

narrator-e4f9692a547e.speaker: narrator
narrator-e4f9692a547e.text: Somewhere far below, a sixth seal stirs. And Malthrax's staff was never found…

narrator-bb25753296aa.speaker: narrator
narrator-bb25753296aa.text: Torchlight gutters on the stair below. Something vast breathes in the dark, and it says your names. Skarn was only the doorman.

brambur-c3e12ddbb572.speaker: brambur
brambur-c3e12ddbb572.text: I'll have a go. For Mum.

fizzwick-12a0a3e5ba30.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-12a0a3e5ba30.text: Fizzwick calculates the pie at forty percent gravy, sixty percent ambition.

brambur-b2500ef3b293.speaker: brambur
brambur-b2500ef3b293.text: Right. Pie can wait. Princess can't.

fizzwick-52973ef9dbe9.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-52973ef9dbe9.text: Fizzwick has prepared a list of reasons to be afraid. It is long. Let us go anyway.

elowen-8f0e24829182.speaker: elowen
elowen-8f0e24829182.text: You found every note. Every single one. I kept writing because I knew you would.

brambur-ddb49db4698b.speaker: brambur
brambur-ddb49db4698b.text: Mum's hammer is going over the fireplace. Next to the pie.

fizzwick-1b9189e7b4da.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-1b9189e7b4da.text: Fizzwick counterspelled a Dread Sovereign. Fizzwick will be insufferable for a decade.

grumsh-0a933308a0af.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-0a933308a0af.text: Final verse: "And the Tyrant fell, and the town sang along, and that is the end of Grumsh's song!"

vexrath-efbcf2ca742f.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-efbcf2ca742f.text: My clan returns to Emberhollow with honour. Thanks to you.

nettle-d83cfb52b0f7.speaker: nettle
nettle-d83cfb52b0f7.text: The tale of the cracked staff. I'll be telling it for years. Badly. With improvements.

elowen-a5e1869bb1f6.speaker: elowen
elowen-a5e1869bb1f6.text: You came. I knew you would.

brambur-19596c9a2062.speaker: brambur
brambur-19596c9a2062.text: I'm having that pie now. All of it.

fizzwick-54509481394c.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-54509481394c.text: Fizzwick will be writing a book. You are in a footnote.

grumsh-68c229913d65.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-68c229913d65.text: Grumsh will finish the ballad. Someday.

vexrath-042b63581cc3.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-042b63581cc3.text: Honour is earned. Today, we earned it.

nettle-e08e51e716e4.speaker: nettle
nettle-e08e51e716e4.text: I'll make this sound even better than it was.

osric-affd9c6db092.speaker: osric
osric-affd9c6db092.text: You carry shadows, child. Hold still... There. The Temple has lifted what clung to you.

rowan-28bc1f5e5324.speaker: rowan
rowan-28bc1f5e5324.text: Hale wrote to me. Said a stranger gave him back his courage. I'd wager that was you. The Watch owes you.

rowan-b5f631e39493.speaker: rowan
rowan-b5f631e39493.text: You brought Hale's name to me. Hard thing to do. I'll see he gets a fair hearing. Thank you.

rowan-7a2881144391.speaker: rowan
rowan-7a2881144391.text: Hale says someone leaned on him down there. I'm not saying it was you. I'm saying I noticed.

marga-956394797cb7.speaker: marga
marga-956394797cb7.text: Funny thing: the scratching under my cellar floor has gone quiet. Rats seem... respectful lately. Is that you? Don't answer.

marga-d79561240e96.speaker: marga
marga-d79561240e96.text: Something's been digging in my cellar all night. They're wearing tiny gold thimbles. Do you know anything about that?

osric-c68d059252f6.speaker: osric
osric-c68d059252f6.text: A drowned soul came to me in a dream, smiling. They say you paid his fare. The Temple blesses you.

osric-eabc82ffee02.speaker: osric
osric-eabc82ffee02.text: The dead keep accounts, child. I pray you balance yours.

wren-76f9a1b6edd1.speaker: wren
wren-76f9a1b6edd1.text: Tobble's back in town! He says you walked him out yourself. Dear heart, I'm making you a tea.

wren-50c08797b15d.speaker: wren
wren-50c08797b15d.text: Tobble says you fed him and let him keep his pride. That's worth more than glowcaps.

wren-ed445890b927.speaker: wren
wren-ed445890b927.text: Tobble came in with an empty pouch and a full heart of anger. I'm not saying anything. I'm saying a very loud nothing.

dobbin-639d0e781f2c.speaker: dobbin
dobbin-639d0e781f2c.text: One strike, they say. One clean strike. That's how it's done.

dobbin-1eec56807604.speaker: dobbin
dobbin-1eec56807604.text: Word is you struck the Silent Anvil twice. Show me your hands, lad. Hm. Steady. Good smithing in those.

dobbin-a7857ae2916b.speaker: dobbin
dobbin-a7857ae2916b.text: You left the old anvil alone. Smart. My grandfather struck it twice. Never did get the shaking out of his hands.

dobbin-a18a367b17a4.speaker: dobbin
dobbin-a18a367b17a4.text: My brothers say a foreman gave them water in the dark. Not forgiveness, mind. But I heard you let him walk. I'll think on it.

dobbin-dc1e3e09cf03.speaker: dobbin
dobbin-dc1e3e09cf03.text: They say the foreman never walked out of the Forge. My brothers were chained by him. I won't weep.

tamsin-63b824041f88.speaker: tamsin
tamsin-63b824041f88.text: Oh, pet. I heard the old horn in my sleep last night. Somebody swore the Warden's oath. Was that you?

tamsin-566f4c019736.speaker: tamsin
tamsin-566f4c019736.text: Somebody swore to guard each other in that vault, pet. Not the town, each other. That's the oath that holds.

tamsin-0cb5dfa8b84e.speaker: tamsin
tamsin-0cb5dfa8b84e.text: The old Warden's gauntlet is gone from the vault, I hear. Well. Everything is for sale in the end. Not everything, pet.

narrator-964b660b23fb.speaker: narrator
narrator-964b660b23fb.text: Sister Vey sinks beneath the water, her hymn ending in bubbles.

narrator-457c3bab8cab.speaker: narrator
narrator-457c3bab8cab.text: Mother Sporegrave collapses into a heap of harmless puffballs.

narrator-23a0f035fd03.speaker: narrator
narrator-23a0f035fd03.text: Skarn tumbles from the Broodmother's back. Among his things: Elowen's ribbon, and a map marked "B2".

narrator-ef47508ef713.speaker: narrator
narrator-ef47508ef713.text: Brambur pries his mother's hammer from Brakk's grip and weeps into his beard.

narrator-e1f5f624efeb.speaker: narrator
narrator-e1f5f624efeb.text: The moon rises over Emberhollow. A seal on the Blackspire cracks and breaks.

narrator-6ca6744a8b32.speaker: narrator
narrator-6ca6744a8b32.text: You cut a bound town guard free. "Captain Rowan sent you? Bless you!"

narrator-3d169bdf9141.speaker: narrator
narrator-3d169bdf9141.text: Lore tablet: "Emberhollow was founded on a sealed tower. The founders buried it, built an inn on top, and agreed never to mention it again."

narrator-8dcbd1afd252.speaker: narrator
narrator-8dcbd1afd252.text: A fresh tunnel, dug straight up toward the Boar & Spoon cellar. You kick out the supports and it caves in. Marga will want to hear.

narrator-d5ae81864589.speaker: narrator
narrator-d5ae81864589.text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 1: "Down in the Warrens where the rat-kings sup, / Grumsh drew his axe and the rats gave up!"

narrator-b4df2862eaa3.speaker: narrator
narrator-b4df2862eaa3.text: Dwarven boot-prints, and a hammer-shaped dent in a rat. "That's Mum's hammer," Brambur whispers. "Someone took it deeper."

narrator-98803d339b3d.speaker: narrator
narrator-98803d339b3d.text: The ceiling here sags over a side-passage where you hear cultists chanting. One good pull would bring it down on them, or on you.

narrator-a8d358051ef2.speaker: narrator
narrator-a8d358051ef2.text: CRACK! The ceiling caves in on the cultist side-passage. Silence, and a pouch of 40 gp rolls out of the dust.

narrator-031e4c35a1b3.speaker: narrator
narrator-031e4c35a1b3.text: A torn spellbook page, covered in Fizzwick's tiny handwriting ("NOTE TO SELF: COUNTERSPELL. ALWAYS COUNTERSPELL.").

narrator-85af568041e5.speaker: narrator
narrator-85af568041e5.text: Half-sunk in the grotto: a satchel stitched with the royal sun. Elowen's temple relics, still dry inside. Brother Osric will want this.

narrator-cee2db010071.speaker: narrator
narrator-cee2db010071.text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 2: "In the Grotto deep where the waters sing, / a lizard with a club tail met a better thing!"

narrator-63269c9ce4eb.speaker: narrator
narrator-63269c9ce4eb.text: Tall tale 1: "The staff was carved from a lightning-struck spire," Nettle writes. "Everyone agrees. Nobody saw it."

narrator-7702f63d140e.speaker: narrator
narrator-7702f63d140e.text: Lore tablet: "The First Warden bound the Tyrant-lizard Gorvax beneath the vault with five seals and a very large horn."

narrator-d407f7b1366b.speaker: narrator
narrator-d407f7b1366b.text: You shatter a humming crystal pylon. Stored dawn-light spills out and sinks into the floor, heading deeper.

narrator-1ca03ad5e1ec.speaker: narrator
narrator-1ca03ad5e1ec.text: A crystal-sealed royal decree. The ORIGINAL. It does not exile Vexrath's clan; it knights them.

narrator-68582edc7c66.speaker: narrator
narrator-68582edc7c66.text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 3: "Through Glimmerdeep's glow where the toadstools scream, / Grumsh screamed louder (it was quite the scene)!"

narrator-09d9696f6da0.speaker: narrator
narrator-09d9696f6da0.text: Tall tale 2: "It hums when he lies," Nettle notes. "So it hums constantly."

narrator-be74ef149940.speaker: narrator
narrator-be74ef149940.text: Lore tablet: "Glimmerdeep crystals drink light. Shatter them and the light they hoarded is set free."

narrator-4f15dbe8682f.speaker: narrator
narrator-4f15dbe8682f.text: You smash the chains of a captive smith. "Tell Dobbin we're coming home, and we'll be at the vault when you need us."

narrator-a98dacac81e9.speaker: narrator
narrator-a98dacac81e9.text: A keg of dwarven blasting powder. Zizzy's eyes light up. "Oh, we are SO using this on the gate."

narrator-bc880204ffdd.speaker: narrator
narrator-bc880204ffdd.text: A keg of dwarven blasting powder. It looks like the sort of thing a sorcerer would enjoy.

narrator-544500ad8657.speaker: narrator
narrator-544500ad8657.text: Zizzy packs the powder against the Ashforge gate. KA-BOOM! The gate, and its guards, are no longer a problem.

narrator-d078d1313e77.speaker: narrator
narrator-d078d1313e77.text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 4: "In Ashforge's heat where the anvils ring, / Grumsh rang louder, being Grumsh, the king!"

narrator-d2121f25121b.speaker: narrator
narrator-d2121f25121b.text: Tall tale 3: "A smith says the staff has a crack near the crystal, mended with cultist spit."

narrator-9fec26629db9.speaker: narrator
narrator-9fec26629db9.text: Lore tablet: "Ashforge was a dwarven forge-hall until Brakk sold it, and its smiths, to the Sovereign."

narrator-fdc59d7476b3.speaker: narrator
narrator-fdc59d7476b3.text: Old Tamsin's tale was true. You will sound it when the Tyrant rises.

narrator-f69e01572ceb.speaker: narrator
narrator-f69e01572ceb.text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 5: "In the Blackspire vault where the Tyrant lay, / [Grumsh: 'Last line comes after we win.']"

narrator-e31ededc2560.speaker: narrator
narrator-e31ededc2560.text: Tall tale 4: "There it is: the crack is under the third ring. Strike there and the whole thing goes." Nettle underlines it twice.

narrator-63d474e31255.speaker: narrator
narrator-63d474e31255.text: Lore tablet: "MALTHRAX. Once court wizard of Emberhollow. Exiled for 'excessive candlelight'. Took it personally."

narrator-d14fe5c055b0.speaker: narrator
narrator-d14fe5c055b0.text: Thimbles, buttons and a wedge of cheese the size of a wagon wheel ring a painted rat in a tiny crown. The rats around it have gone very quiet. All of them are looking at you.

narrator-a444406f20fc.speaker: narrator
narrator-a444406f20fc.text: The thimbles are heavy, bright gold. Somewhere inside the walls, a thousand tiny feet start moving.

narrator-ae1979452ae5.speaker: narrator
narrator-ae1979452ae5.text: You set a coin before the crown. The rats bow. Truly. The tunnels feel quieter.

narrator-f3845bbaa402.speaker: narrator
narrator-f3845bbaa402.text: It is alarmingly good cheese. Pip is moved to tears. Everyone feels rested and oddly proud.

narrator-b63b65c74f84.speaker: narrator
narrator-b63b65c74f84.text: A guardsman in a scorched Watch tabard sits wedged in a niche, sword across his knees. "Corporal Hale," he mumbles. "I ran. When the cultists came, I ran. I can't go back to the Captain. I can't."

narrator-5c946cfbd148.speaker: narrator
narrator-5c946cfbd148.text: "Thank you. I'll tell Rowan myself." He straightens a little, tabard and all. You feel like you did something that matters.

narrator-9e1ea6c307c8.speaker: narrator
narrator-9e1ea6c307c8.text: He closes his eyes and nods. "Fair." You note his name and leave him his sword. Duty is a heavy coat.

narrator-783d1f1e2310.speaker: narrator
narrator-783d1f1e2310.text: He hands over a battered pouch without meeting your eyes. It stings a little, taking it.

narrator-57e949c96bdf.speaker: narrator
narrator-57e949c96bdf.text: A bronze bell hangs half-sunk in a black pool, its rope trailing underwater. It tolls once, very softly, though nothing touched it.

narrator-cf7c3c554cb6.speaker: narrator
narrator-cf7c3c554cb6.text: Each toll rolls out across the water. Something far away answers, then thinks better of it. You feel rather wiser, and rather watched.

narrator-4602e73b5ac2.speaker: narrator
narrator-4602e73b5ac2.text: Cold hands find a clapper of pearl-white bone-metal. It hums in your palm: a fortune charm, still warm.

narrator-b5287295d618.speaker: narrator
narrator-b5287295d618.text: The water is deeper than it looks. You scramble out, coughing, with nothing but a bruise and a lesson.

narrator-86fae8805258.speaker: narrator
narrator-86fae8805258.text: The bell sighs out one last quiet note, as if relieved. Brambur prays for it.

narrator-033d4b235109.speaker: narrator
narrator-033d4b235109.text: A drowned ferryman sits in a rotted skiff, one dripping hand held out. "Thirty years I have waited for a fare," he says. "Pay, and I may finally sleep."

narrator-69172414a384.speaker: narrator
narrator-69172414a384.text: He bows. The skiff slides gently under the black water, and in the ripples lies a pearl the size of a plum.

narrator-dd4bf1c99b90.speaker: narrator
narrator-dd4bf1c99b90.text: The words come true and quiet. He sighs, smiles, and the skiff goes down with him. The tunnels feel safer.

narrator-04ecab46717e.speaker: narrator
narrator-04ecab46717e.text: He listens to the whole prayer, kindly. "A good try," he says. "I will wait a little longer." He gives you a nod.

narrator-e2505dbb5463.speaker: narrator
narrator-e2505dbb5463.text: You find a cache of waterlogged coins. The ferryman watches you without a word. It is somehow the worst part.

narrator-e679e3912e9e.speaker: narrator
narrator-e679e3912e9e.text: A tall crystal shows each of you as you truly are: braver, kinder and a little more frightened than you thought. It hums, waiting.

narrator-d120d2f804c6.speaker: narrator
narrator-d120d2f804c6.text: You each see what you are. Nobody speaks for a while, but everyone feels clearer. A strange new steadiness settles over the party.

narrator-69944d6965e1.speaker: narrator
narrator-69944d6965e1.text: The shards are worth a small fortune. The purse in your pocket feels suspiciously lighter afterwards.

narrator-dc886e55bc1c.speaker: narrator
narrator-dc886e55bc1c.text: The facets are tuned like a harp. You find a seam, and a small lens of mirror-glass comes away in your hand.

narrator-6834d5076e2d.speaker: narrator
narrator-6834d5076e2d.text: The crystal gives you a headache, and a very smug reflection of yourself. That is all.

narrator-2657638dbce0.speaker: narrator
narrator-2657638dbce0.text: A gnome with a lantern for a hat huddles in a crystal seam, sobbing into a pouch of glowing mushrooms. "Tobble Grindlewick!" he sniffles. "I sell glowcaps to the herbalist in Emberhollow! I got lost three days ago!"

narrator-437d34b55b98.speaker: narrator
narrator-437d34b55b98.text: It takes a while, and a little shouting. Tobble hugs your boots and runs for the surface. You feel good about it.

narrator-6418ae6cacf3.speaker: narrator
narrator-6418ae6cacf3.text: He eats everything, thanks you with enormous dignity, and gives you a bundle of the best glowcaps. "For the herbalist. Or you."

narrator-1cfa2a4ceeb3.speaker: narrator
narrator-1cfa2a4ceeb3.text: It is heavy and bright. He does not stop you. You realise a bit late that he is looking at you as if you were a monster.

narrator-7b7c4956ffc3.speaker: narrator
narrator-7b7c4956ffc3.text: An anvil older than the Forge stands in a ring of cold ash, a hammer laid across its face. Words are cut into the iron: STRIKE ONCE FOR STRENGTH. STRIKE TWICE FOR FEAR.

narrator-ed9868da6eeb.speaker: narrator
narrator-ed9868da6eeb.text: A single clear note rings out of the iron. Your hands steady, and the next chest you open will feel lucky.

narrator-c48ad6156c92.speaker: narrator
narrator-c48ad6156c92.text: The second ring is wrong: deep and hungry. It gives you something precious and takes something less visible. The dead stir in the walls.

narrator-8bde43e09553.speaker: narrator
narrator-8bde43e09553.text: You lay the hammer neatly across the anvil. A faint warmth follows you: respect, from something old. A flask of tempering oil appears at your feet.

narrator-57544376a96c.speaker: narrator
narrator-57544376a96c.text: A burned cultist foreman kneels beside a cooling channel, sobbing. "Mercy. I only held the keys. I never struck them. Let me go, and I will tell you where the smiths are held."

narrator-8988a7a90949.speaker: narrator
narrator-8988a7a90949.text: He gives you the keys and a hurried map of the lower forges. He bolts for the stairs, and a quiet nod from the party says you were right.

narrator-15e9b8004f7e.speaker: narrator
narrator-15e9b8004f7e.text: He swears on his mother, his mother's mother and the keys. He leaves, and you leave with his purse.

narrator-641769690226.speaker: narrator
narrator-641769690226.text: He laughs, hysterical, and darts away into the dark. The keys remain, but his promise does not.

narrator-e2c99e753735.speaker: narrator
narrator-e2c99e753735.text: It is quick and ugly. His keys are good keys, and his purse is heavy. Nobody says anything for a while.

narrator-7c72453111a0.speaker: narrator
narrator-7c72453111a0.text: A weathered statue of a Warden stands with open hands. At its feet a cracked plate reads: WHO KEEPS THE SEALS KEEPS THE TOWN. A faint horn-note hangs in the air.

narrator-a95d7310e88b.speaker: narrator
narrator-a95d7310e88b.text: The statue's hands close, just slightly, around yours. Warmth floods the party, and the hush of a good road settles around you.

narrator-6b245607b470.speaker: narrator
narrator-6b245607b470.text: Four voices, one oath. The statue's head tilts, almost fondly. The bond of the party tightens.

narrator-d15f539c0ef7.speaker: narrator
narrator-d15f539c0ef7.text: It comes away with a groan of old iron. Even as you lift it, you know the vault is going to remember this.

narrator-bb9e0f1affb3.speaker: narrator
narrator-bb9e0f1affb3.text: A cracked seal in the wall breathes a voice like warm oil. "Little knights. I can make you stronger. I ask only for a small favour."

narrator-937ed955c827.speaker: narrator
narrator-937ed955c827.text: Power pours into your hand. Something cold settles into your purse, and the dead begin to turn in their sleep.

narrator-d0e80565330c.speaker: narrator
narrator-d0e80565330c.text: The seal sputters, outraged. Nerves steady across the party, and the vault seems to wince.

narrator-b8e2b5e8f569.speaker: narrator
narrator-b8e2b5e8f569.text: Scratched into the wall: "SKARN RIDES THE SPIDER QUEEN. THE RUSTY KEY OPENS HER DEN."

narrator-527ffbd1e728.speaker: narrator
narrator-527ffbd1e728.text: A faded mural shows a lizard as big as a cathedral. Someone has drawn a mustache on it.

narrator-0ab37f479651.speaker: narrator
narrator-0ab37f479651.text: Dripping water spells nothing in particular. Brambur apologizes to it anyway.

narrator-85883228ce39.speaker: narrator
narrator-85883228ce39.text: An inscription: "BEYOND THE CORAL DOOR SLEEPS OLD CLUBTAIL. BRING SNACKS."

narrator-d6e67426a1bb.speaker: narrator
narrator-d6e67426a1bb.text: A cracked mirror. Professor Fizzwick spends some time admiring it.

narrator-ccf374b26192.speaker: narrator
narrator-ccf374b26192.text: The crystals here show your reflection a half-second late. Fizzwick waves at his. It waves back early.

narrator-14d0ffd63442.speaker: narrator
narrator-14d0ffd63442.text: Scratched in a crystal: "DO NOT LOOK THE LIZARD IN THE EYE. USE A MIRROR. a statue, probably"

narrator-964677ae5c65.speaker: narrator
narrator-964677ae5c65.text: A circle of mushrooms. Grumsh steps in it and refuses to say what he saw.

narrator-75d75fc1ae12.speaker: narrator
narrator-75d75fc1ae12.text: An anvil, still warm, with a smith's name scratched on it: "VARR".

narrator-3713fc56ea26.speaker: narrator
narrator-3713fc56ea26.text: A forge-mural: dwarves, a chimera, and a very small Brakk hiding behind it.

narrator-730bd18f9b7e.speaker: narrator
narrator-730bd18f9b7e.text: A sign: "BRAKK'S FORGE. NO REFUNDS. NO DWARVES. NO CHIMERA-PETTING."

narrator-20b6802e4a33.speaker: narrator
narrator-20b6802e4a33.text: Carved in gold: "HE WHO TAKES THE DAWNSTONE AMULET SHALL HOLD THE FIVE SEALS."

narrator-de7856d9d686.speaker: narrator
narrator-de7856d9d686.text: Enormous footprints. Fizzwick measures one. "Fizzwick estimates: large."

narrator-1823753fe18e.speaker: narrator
narrator-1823753fe18e.text: A shrine to a forgotten god of cutlery. Pip weeps openly.

narrator-58c024482a81.speaker: narrator
narrator-58c024482a81.text: Scratched into the stone: "The wardens fed the rats first, so the rats would learn to love the dark. They did."

narrator-b8906c2669ea.speaker: narrator
narrator-b8906c2669ea.text: A child's tally of days, 41 marks, then a drawing of a door.

narrator-c1925c67caf2.speaker: narrator
narrator-c1925c67caf2.text: A drowned scribe left a note: "The water was never a flood. It was a door the Tyrant wanted shut."

narrator-139a53db5dfa.speaker: narrator
narrator-139a53db5dfa.text: Pressed flowers, long dried: someone kept a garden down here.

narrator-05594a4b6f9b.speaker: narrator
narrator-05594a4b6f9b.text: Crystal-etched verse: "Glass remembers every face that looked into it. Do not look long."

narrator-6b41bd1bc0c1.speaker: narrator
narrator-6b41bd1bc0c1.text: A map fragment with a single mark: "The Warden sleeps standing."

narrator-46effa2a4319.speaker: narrator
narrator-46effa2a4319.text: Forge-script: "Every blade of Ashforge was quenched in a prisoner's name. Brakk kept the list."

narrator-4cc85d731a08.speaker: narrator
narrator-4cc85d731a08.text: A small hammer, wrapped in cloth. No name on it.

narrator-2829e31de58c.speaker: narrator
narrator-2829e31de58c.text: Carved over the lintel: "Gorvax was not the first thing to rule here. He is simply the loudest."

narrator-a95eb0f97eaf.speaker: narrator
narrator-a95eb0f97eaf.text: A saddle-strap, thunder-lizard hide. Someone rode these once.

narrator-d4d80f58f92c.speaker: narrator
narrator-d4d80f58f92c.text: The camp is quiet. Too quiet.

narrator-3ed82cf32abb.speaker: narrator
narrator-3ed82cf32abb.text: Back in the Rat-Warrens. The scratching starts up again.

narrator-f5c72615823b.speaker: narrator
narrator-f5c72615823b.text: The Drowned Grotto. Cold water closes over your boots once more.

narrator-27beacd47762.speaker: narrator
narrator-27beacd47762.text: The Glimmerdeep hums its single note. Your reflections are waiting.

narrator-92bfd56cf939.speaker: narrator
narrator-92bfd56cf939.text: The Ashforge heat greets you like an old, bad-tempered friend.

narrator-be06dc8a2a14.speaker: narrator
narrator-be06dc8a2a14.text: The Vault. The breathing has not stopped.

narrator-00a876dd1952.speaker: narrator
narrator-00a876dd1952.text: Here the rat-sign stops, as if even the vermin give this spot a wide berth. Something waits here that is not a rat.

narrator-fdeddfde6919.speaker: narrator
narrator-fdeddfde6919.text: Clear water bubbles from a cracked basin carved with a smiling face. It smells, astonishingly, of mint.

narrator-b4d1c4c33c02.speaker: narrator
narrator-b4d1c4c33c02.text: A spiral stair corkscrews down into the dark. A cold draught rises from it, carrying the smell of standing water.

narrator-e7b40c694e6a.speaker: narrator
narrator-e7b40c694e6a.text: The hidden passage is lined with tiny claw-marked tallies. Someone, or several someones, has been counting days here.

narrator-327b80946f51.speaker: narrator
narrator-327b80946f51.text: A low chamber stacked with mouldy grain sacks, every one of them gnawed open. The floor crunches underfoot, and you decide not to look down.

narrator-8d398a0537ca.speaker: narrator
narrator-8d398a0537ca.text: Water pools in the middle of this chamber, and the walls are furred with nests of shredded cloth. The smell is magnificent, in the worst way.

narrator-d9f30bfe51c0.speaker: narrator
narrator-d9f30bfe51c0.text: Old smuggler's crates rot in the corners, stamped with the crest of Emberhollow. One still rattles faintly when you pass.

narrator-9d6badccf754.speaker: narrator
narrator-9d6badccf754.text: A ring of half-sunken lanterns marks this place, each one still somehow burning beneath the water.

narrator-ed9ae9d40880.speaker: narrator
narrator-ed9ae9d40880.text: A spring of warm, glowing water rises here, fizzing gently. The fungus around it grows in the shape of open hands.

narrator-e09c7b2b93d5.speaker: narrator
narrator-e09c7b2b93d5.text: Steps slick with algae lead down past a waterline carved with the warning "HIGH TIDE". The ink is fresh.

narrator-8a9ebb9efd23.speaker: narrator
narrator-8a9ebb9efd23.text: Behind the false wall is a dry pocket of air that smells of old parchment. Someone hid here while the water rose.

narrator-0569952d3f06.speaker: narrator
narrator-0569952d3f06.text: A flooded hall where bioluminescent eels drift between broken columns, lighting the water in slow blue pulses.

narrator-8e51f5cf02f0.speaker: narrator
narrator-8e51f5cf02f0.text: Shipwreck timbers jut from the walls of this cave, though the sea is miles away. A barnacled figurehead watches you pass.

narrator-c7450fdaf8aa.speaker: narrator
narrator-c7450fdaf8aa.text: Stalactites drip in this grotto like a broken water clock. The pools below are full of tiny white crabs that click in unison.

narrator-9a1ea6db9271.speaker: narrator
narrator-9a1ea6db9271.text: Nets heavy with old catches hang from the ceiling here. Some of the catches are wearing boots.

narrator-75f9ddc8e0b8.speaker: narrator
narrator-75f9ddc8e0b8.text: The hum of the crystals drops to a low, almost-words murmur here, as if the cavern is trying to tell you something.

narrator-ae00794a10da.speaker: narrator
narrator-ae00794a10da.text: A pool of liquid starlight shimmers in a crystal bowl. Drinking it tastes like the first cold breath of winter.

narrator-7de588c09d6b.speaker: narrator
narrator-7de588c09d6b.text: A crystal stair spirals downward, each step chiming a note as you test it. The tune is not a happy one.

narrator-22e454f641f3.speaker: narrator
narrator-22e454f641f3.text: The concealed grotto is dark: no crystals, no reflections, no hum. The silence is the loudest thing you have heard all day.

narrator-bc62f88d53d3.speaker: narrator
narrator-bc62f88d53d3.text: A gallery of statues frozen mid-stride, each one carrying a mirror that was raised a moment too late.

narrator-369fdb67673f.speaker: narrator
narrator-369fdb67673f.text: Huge amethyst columns split the light into slow purple rainbows. The floor is warm, and faintly ticks like cooling glass.

narrator-ac3d17dd266b.speaker: narrator
narrator-ac3d17dd266b.text: A garden of luminous mushrooms grows in a perfect spiral here. Stepping off the path makes them all turn to face you.

narrator-e000cba1c7c8.speaker: narrator
narrator-e000cba1c7c8.text: Shards of a shattered geode the size of a cottage litter this chamber, still humming with whatever broke out of it.

narrator-0e20c41ef8de.speaker: narrator
narrator-0e20c41ef8de.text: Here the hammer-song stops. Tools lie where they were dropped, mid-swing, and the air smells of a hasty departure.

narrator-449c0988ab03.speaker: narrator
narrator-449c0988ab03.text: Cool water pours from the mouth of a stone dwarf into a quenching trough. Steam curls up, smelling of iron and relief.

narrator-53ab77840203.speaker: narrator
narrator-53ab77840203.text: A brass-railed stair plunges into dark heat. Each step down is a little warmer, and the walls start to sweat.

narrator-02eb08231bba.speaker: narrator
narrator-02eb08231bba.text: A hidden smithy, its tools neatly hung and its coals banked as if the smith stepped out for lunch a hundred years ago.

narrator-e63192e04923.speaker: narrator
narrator-e63192e04923.text: A chamber of cooling moulds, each one shaped like a different weapon. Several of the moulds are empty and still warm.

narrator-f32bc1223e42.speaker: narrator
narrator-f32bc1223e42.text: Bellows the size of houses wheeze in this hall, pushed by nothing you can see. Embers dance in the draught.

narrator-9dc1240b2637.speaker: narrator
narrator-9dc1240b2637.text: An ore-cart track loops through this cavern, and a cart full of glowing slag still creaks slowly along it.

narrator-93c7575fa67e.speaker: narrator
narrator-93c7575fa67e.text: Racks of half-finished armour line the walls here, helmets turned so that every empty visor watches the door.

narrator-4f41071a3f73.speaker: narrator
narrator-4f41071a3f73.text: Old murals here show tiny heroes fleeing a towering lizard. The last panel has been scratched out with claws.

narrator-9bc1cef621ce.speaker: narrator
narrator-9bc1cef621ce.text: A basin of violet light pulses slowly, like a resting heartbeat. The pain of the road drains away as you drink.

narrator-87cdec04142e.speaker: narrator
narrator-87cdec04142e.text: Elowen's light pours from the altar ahead, golden and steady. Five keyholes wait around its rim.

narrator-c9384da7cdcf.speaker: narrator
narrator-c9384da7cdcf.text: This hidden alcove holds the bones of a knight in mirrored armour, one hand still pointing toward the vault.

narrator-a77256f6cb40.speaker: narrator
narrator-a77256f6cb40.text: Eggshells as big as barrels lie cracked open across this chamber. Whatever hatched has had a long time to grow.

narrator-73bd2dd724d8.speaker: narrator
narrator-73bd2dd724d8.text: Carved pillars of roaring lizards hold up a ceiling lost in darkness. Rain-sound echoes from far above, though there is no sky.

narrator-639a646642ca.speaker: narrator
narrator-639a646642ca.text: A trophy hall of crushed shields and bent swords, each tagged with a name in neat, patient handwriting.

narrator-8bba228827e7.speaker: narrator
narrator-8bba228827e7.text: The floor here is scorched in a long, perfect line, as if lightning once ran along it on four legs.

narrator-dec8958b1c1e.speaker: narrator
narrator-dec8958b1c1e.text: Emberhollow huddles in the long shadow of the Blackspire, a jumble of slate roofs and leaning chimneys. The square smells of woodsmoke and hot pies, and a bell tolls the hour a little nervously. Townsfolk hurry past, glancing at the dark tower the way you glance at a sleeping dog. Everyone here has lost someone to the maze.

narrator-8f8a670b8d08.speaker: narrator
narrator-8f8a670b8d08.text: The Boar & Spoon is warm, loud and smells of spilled ale, roast onions and wet dog. A fiddler saws at something cheerful in the corner while a mounted boar's head, wearing a spoon on a string, watches the door. Adventurers swap tall tales at long tables, and every one of them has a story about the Blackspire.

narrator-28f49355f55e.speaker: narrator
narrator-28f49355f55e.text: The Temple of Cant is cool and hushed, lit by tall candles that never quite drip. Incense of cedar and myrrh drifts past a donation box the size of a coffin. Somewhere a priest is counting coins very quietly.

narrator-8bd3cbc0ad78.speaker: narrator
narrator-8bd3cbc0ad78.text: Straw dummies hang from posts in the Training Grounds, most of them missing their heads. The air rings with clashing steel, barked orders and the thud of arrows striking targets. A grizzled sergeant watches you sideways and mutters something about soft hands.

narrator-ae9bdf17af22.speaker: narrator
narrator-ae9bdf17af22.text: Fizzbang's Trading Post is an avalanche of goods waiting to happen: ropes, lanterns, potions and at least one suspicious barrel. It smells of lamp oil and lavender soap. A gnome peers at you over a counter piled high with "bargains".

narrator-a0714f6b37db.speaker: narrator
narrator-a0714f6b37db.text: The cobbles end at a ring of standing stones around a gaping stair. Cold air breathes up from below, carrying faint echoes: a drip, a scratch, something like distant laughter. The town's last lantern swings above the entrance, and nobody has ever bothered to light it.

vp_wiseelder-2099cfe37782.speaker: vp_wiseelder
vp_wiseelder-2099cfe37782.text: Ah, you have need of me?

vp_nobleknight-9f4185e76409.speaker: vp_nobleknight
vp_nobleknight-9f4185e76409.text: In the name of the Crown!

vp_nobleknight-df47c706efa6.speaker: vp_nobleknight
vp_nobleknight-df47c706efa6.text: A blow worthy of a song!

vp_nobleknight-aeea520143c9.speaker: vp_nobleknight
vp_nobleknight-aeea520143c9.text: I am worthy of the oath.

vp_nobleknight-e1540dc307a2.speaker: vp_nobleknight
vp_nobleknight-e1540dc307a2.text: I will stand to the last.

vp_cheerfulbard-ffad21eee31f.speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
vp_cheerfulbard-ffad21eee31f.text: And a one, and a two!

vp_cheerfulbard-9d76a38d6d2a.speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
vp_cheerfulbard-9d76a38d6d2a.text: Ooh, that is a sour note.

vp_cheerfulbard-25147bbf4dda.speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
vp_cheerfulbard-25147bbf4dda.text: That is a ballad, right there!

vp_cheerfulbard-e8dd14179f28.speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
vp_cheerfulbard-e8dd14179f28.text: No no no, not the finale!

vp_dourdwarf-fbb94a1efa70.speaker: vp_dourdwarf
vp_dourdwarf-fbb94a1efa70.text: I have had worse. Not much worse.

vp_dourdwarf-abf023e12f1a.speaker: vp_dourdwarf
vp_dourdwarf-abf023e12f1a.text: I do not like magic. Fine.

vp_dourdwarf-7297b80d1dfe.speaker: vp_dourdwarf
vp_dourdwarf-7297b80d1dfe.text: I knew it. I knew it.

vp_boomingbarbarian-b03146c62952.speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
vp_boomingbarbarian-b03146c62952.text: Tell my axe... I loved it.

pip-b00c9079d23f.speaker: pip
pip-b00c9079d23f.text: Don't touch that. That is the Lantern Row mark. My crew's. We left it wherever it was safe to leave things.

pip-f8bc6a0d384a.speaker: pip
pip-f8bc6a0d384a.text: G. Vane. Garrick Vane. He crosses his sevens like a man signing a death warrant. Three years I have wondered who sold us. Now I have a name, and a handwriting. Thank you for not making it a speech.

pip-07fa51dce30b.speaker: pip
pip-07fa51dce30b.text: Garrick. Of course it is Garrick. He always bought cheap paper. It is the one thing I would have trusted him on.

pip-620f7fb7b92e.speaker: pip
pip-620f7fb7b92e.text: That is her boat. I painted it. Badly. She said it looked like a pudding. She named it herself, at seven years old, and she had opinions.

pip-bbf43ac35bf1.speaker: pip
pip-bbf43ac35bf1.text: Unharmed. Alive. She was alive. Excuse me. Something in my eye. The dungeon is very dusty.

pip-1671107f5924.speaker: pip
pip-1671107f5924.text: She wore one just like it. Either they took her, or she lost it. I would like to believe the first. It is the better story.

pip-24d741e8a86a.speaker: pip
pip-24d741e8a86a.text: That is a tithe ledger. Names and prices. I know this hand. I would know it in the dark.

pip-10aa13ed3149.speaker: pip
pip-10aa13ed3149.text: Seneschal. A title and a ring of keys, for eleven of us. And he kept her. Three years he has kept her, to make sure I stayed quiet.

pip-8c9f8b9eace0.speaker: pip
pip-8c9f8b9eace0.text: Seneschal. Fancy. I would have given him a better title. Several.

pip-939c65ce8719.speaker: pip
pip-939c65ce8719.text: A master key, Lantern Row pattern. He is having them copied. He is making himself a way out. Coward.

pip-32c004f30c28.speaker: pip
pip-32c004f30c28.text: G.V. In the bow. He signs his keys. Vain to the end.

pip-e43a35e9a065.speaker: pip
pip-e43a35e9a065.text: Close enough. I know his handwriting. I know his keys. I will know his face when I see it.

pip-49de12fa4535.speaker: pip
pip-49de12fa4535.text: Eleven notches. One for each of us. He kept them. Garrick keeps everything. Sentimental. It is the worst thing about him.

garrick-093efeefd841.speaker: garrick
garrick-093efeefd841.text: Pip. You are late. I had you down for two winters ago. Do sit. Everyone sits eventually.

pip-5c04eb680d82.speaker: pip
pip-5c04eb680d82.text: Hello, Garrick. You have gone grey. It suits you. It is the first honest thing you have worn.

garrick-617df18eefa3.speaker: garrick
garrick-617df18eefa3.text: Come now. It was only business. The Row was never going to survive the Sovereign. I chose the winning side, and sold what was already lost.

pip-8e71bd004cbb.speaker: pip
pip-8e71bd004cbb.text: You sold eleven of us. And my sister.

garrick-f07fff9c673f.speaker: garrick
garrick-f07fff9c673f.text: She is not in the ash, Pip. I did that much. I did that much, and you may hate me for the rest.

garrick-bd5bbc797e20.speaker: garrick
garrick-bd5bbc797e20.text: She burned with the others. I am sorry. I think of her every day. I think of her often.

garrick-eb00bfc90422.speaker: garrick
garrick-eb00bfc90422.text: Well. You have been thorough. Very well. She is not dead. I hid her before the fire. I was never a good man, Pip. I was a careful one.

pip-6348be5a895b.speaker: pip
pip-6348be5a895b.text: It is your call. It was always going to be your call. I just want you to know I have already made up my mind.

pip-55e70f22c244.speaker: pip
pip-55e70f22c244.text: That is it? Three years. That is all there was?

pip-c7b0e69faab3.speaker: pip
pip-c7b0e69faab3.text: He took her with him. Of course he did. I will find her. It will just take longer.

pip-59fe79b31391.speaker: pip
pip-59fe79b31391.text: Keep the gold. I will take the dagger, and the ledger. Someone should remember their names.

pip-cd411c22e680.speaker: pip
pip-cd411c22e680.text: I heard you. I am sorry. I could not do it your way.

pip-730c6ea7a148.speaker: pip
pip-730c6ea7a148.text: Fine. Fine! I hate this. I am letting him live because you asked, not because he deserves it.

garrick-3f119251ba32.speaker: garrick
garrick-3f119251ba32.text: Posy is alive. She is in Emberhollow, a lamplighter's apprentice on Cant Street, under the name Pell. And here is something you do not know. The Sovereign's staff has a crack beneath the third ring. Strike there, and the whole thing shatters.

odalys-1982396fcc7d.speaker: odalys
odalys-1982396fcc7d.text: Shut the door. Quickly. Someone is selling cult silver in Emberhollow, temple candlesticks with the Blackspire sigil filed off, and every pawn ticket bears my name. I never wrote them.

odalys-fac7ac769c46.speaker: odalys
odalys-fac7ac769c46.text: Captain Rowan will see a cult fence, not a victim, if he sees those tickets before I clear this. Find who is forging my hand, and I will make it worth your while.

odalys-3b29f12fe62e.speaker: odalys
odalys-3b29f12fe62e.text: Because Rowan would hang the nearest thief and call it justice. I have pawned since I was fourteen. I know how magistrates think.

tuck-556bae390db8.speaker: tuck
tuck-556bae390db8.text: Bit late for a stroll, friends. Looking for someone to bury?

tuck-eb4571cb9229.speaker: tuck
tuck-eb4571cb9229.text: It was the candlesticks. The old spares, sat in the crypt since before the Sovereign. Nobody counts the dead's candlesticks. I owe three months rent, and my wife is poorly. I used Mistress Fenn's name because it was the only name a pawnbroker would trust. I am sorry. I am so sorry.

odalys-e9e2b2ec37dc.speaker: odalys
odalys-e9e2b2ec37dc.text: Justice is done. It feels like less than I had hoped. Take the cloak. It was never redeemed.

tuck-bfc3aa57bdbf.speaker: tuck
tuck-bfc3aa57bdbf.text: I will dig your garden and sweep your shop, Mistress, for a year and a day. And I will pay back every coin.

odalys-319765efdbac.speaker: odalys
odalys-319765efdbac.text: A year and a day. And you tell no one where you found those candlesticks. I would like the Temple to go on believing that crypt is sealed.

odalys-457bee0bd378.speaker: odalys
odalys-457bee0bd378.text: Well. The thieving stops, at least. I will cover the tickets myself. Take something for your trouble.

odalys-9a1746131fd1.speaker: odalys
odalys-9a1746131fd1.text: I did not see that, and I did not hear that, and we will never speak of it. Here. Your half of the quiet.

tuck-6bb4c87075fa.speaker: tuck
tuck-6bb4c87075fa.text: No. I have buried better folk than you. Go on, tell the Captain. See if he believes a pawnbroker's ledger over a gravedigger's word.

odalys-effad7f48bab.speaker: odalys
odalys-effad7f48bab.text: Well? The tickets will not forge themselves, though someone seems determined to try.

odalys-b02228e85579.speaker: odalys
odalys-b02228e85579.text: Fenn and Daughters remembers a kindness. Come back any time. There is always a bargain behind the counter.

harl-08b81bbc2eb8.speaker: harl
harl-08b81bbc2eb8.text: You are the ones going down. Aye. My wife Anselma led the Sisters of the Tide, fourteen voices, every dusk at the old shrine in the grotto. The cult came for the shrine. The Sisters went down to sing, and never came up.

harl-6823c245673a.speaker: harl
harl-6823c245673a.text: Some nights I hear them through the cellar wall, singing the Evening Hymn, only slower. Find out what happened. Bring me my wife, or bring me the truth. I will take either.

harl-c68a36ecff61.speaker: harl
harl-c68a36ecff61.text: The tide is still turning. Any word of Anselma?

harl-354522e66a32.speaker: harl
harl-354522e66a32.text: She is free? Truly free? Then I will sleep tonight. It is not much, but it is hers: Anselma's mantle, and every coin I could scrape. She would say you should have a hot meal.

harl-50e1dd032a1b.speaker: harl
harl-50e1dd032a1b.text: She is still singing. Still down there. You made a bell of my wife.

harl-cecf55339abb.speaker: harl
harl-cecf55339abb.text: Take your silver and go. I will not say it was wrong. I will not say thank you either.

harl-f0767f134f4a.speaker: harl
harl-f0767f134f4a.text: The nets are full again, and some evenings I sing the hymn myself. Badly. She would laugh.

harl-cb27c6af89fd.speaker: harl
harl-cb27c6af89fd.text: I hear her through the cellar wall, still. I do not go down there.

anselma-7199a44881a0.speaker: anselma
anselma-7199a44881a0.text: Do not let Harl come down. Please. He will wade in after me, and the Pool will keep him too. Tell him I am not afraid. Tell him I lied.

anselma-16d57108ab75.speaker: anselma
anselma-16d57108ab75.text: Harl. Is that Harl? No. Thank the Tide. Listen. The Sisters are bound to the bell. The cult did it to hold the grotto water back from the vault, and we have sung until we forgot we may stop. I cannot stop on my own.

anselma-df21bda8d2da.speaker: anselma
anselma-df21bda8d2da.text: Thank you. Tell Harl the brooch is his. Tell him to go fishing.

ysolde-ef6fc76e37f0.speaker: ysolde
ysolde-ef6fc76e37f0.text: Do not shine that at me. They bring lights, and then they bring questions. Are you the heroes the cult keeps whispering about? The ones who killed Skarn?

ysolde-a0fbe8d9ed0e.speaker: ysolde
ysolde-a0fbe8d9ed0e.text: Ysolde Verrin. Third generation, Glimmerdeep Glassworks. The cult took us all for the Sovereign's commission: a mirror, tall as a door, to watch whoever came down the stair. I ground the lens. I am so sorry. It is in the old kiln, east of here, and it is looking at you right now.

ysolde-450192857714.speaker: ysolde
ysolde-450192857714.text: Break it, or learn from it. I will not tell you which. A glasswright learns what a mirror costs, and I have paid. Go to the kiln. I will wait here. I am very good at waiting.

ysolde-5056bcbebca5.speaker: ysolde
ysolde-5056bcbebca5.text: Fine. Ysolde Verrin, glasswright. I made the cult a scrying mirror, under duress, and it stands in the old kiln east of here. It watches. Break it or use it. I just want it gone from my sight.

ysolde-ca1d2e752175.speaker: ysolde
ysolde-ca1d2e752175.text: Well? The kiln is east. Do not look into it too long. It is rude, and it looks back.

malthrax-787c4370f625.speaker: malthrax
malthrax-787c4370f625.text: Little heroes. I have been waiting.

ysolde-fcc0da8808a9.speaker: ysolde
ysolde-fcc0da8808a9.text: It is quiet. The glass hums no more. Take this. Verrin glass, ground for you. It will keep the world's tricks out of your eyes.

ysolde-2a30c9ae9051.speaker: ysolde
ysolde-2a30c9ae9051.text: You looked. Of course you looked. Everyone looks. I will not lecture. I will only say the Mirror still stands, and it knows your faces now. Be quick.

crane-a6e5105df9da.speaker: crane
crane-a6e5105df9da.text: Halt. Name and watch. No. You are not Watch. You are too loud and too alive.

crane-69c52adc7134.speaker: crane
crane-69c52adc7134.text: Sergeant Aldous Crane, Warden's Watch, Fourth Company. I call the roll every night, and every night three names do not answer. Corporal Dunstan Hale. Private Ilsa Marn. Private Joss Kettering. I cannot rest until I know where they lie, and why the seals fell on my watch.

crane-0b82e95fc795.speaker: crane
crane-0b82e95fc795.text: Then you have my thanks, and my sword arm, if the dead can lend one. They will be deeper. The Fourth's barracks were on the vault level. Look for our tags.

crane-8ac67ad83667.speaker: crane
crane-8ac67ad83667.text: You have found them. I see it in how you stand. Tell me, then. Where did Dunstan Hale fall, and who opened my seals?

crane-8ddc96e044aa.speaker: crane
crane-8ddc96e044aa.text: Fragments. I will not hang a dead man on fragments. Come back with more, or with a kinder story.

crane-9e43bceeb9ca.speaker: crane
crane-9e43bceeb9ca.text: Do not lie to a sergeant. I have heard a thousand excuses from better liars than you.

crane-b334ad80acba.speaker: crane
crane-b334ad80acba.text: Dunstan. My oldest friend. I would have given him my own pay. Thank you. I would rather know. A man should know who he held the line beside.

crane-cb9cd08a88be.speaker: crane
crane-cb9cd08a88be.text: I will stand with you at the end, if you will have me. Hold the line.

crane-104a7c107910.speaker: crane
crane-104a7c107910.text: To the last. Yes. That sounds like Dunstan. I will tell the others he held the line.

pip-132aff1e4c5a.speaker: pip
pip-132aff1e4c5a.text: Another fight. Finally, someone who says what they mean.

pip-a7425e3ece4c.speaker: pip
pip-a7425e3ece4c.text: Stay behind me. Not because I'm brave. Because I'm cheaper to replace.

pip-a46956abaa14.speaker: pip
pip-a46956abaa14.text: One down. A few thousand grudges to go.

pip-bc29eb28fff0.speaker: pip
pip-bc29eb28fff0.text: Don't look so surprised. I've had practice.

pip-86d00b02a077.speaker: pip
pip-86d00b02a077.text: Right between the ribs. I'd say sorry, but I'd be lying.

pip-0d69d96acf26.speaker: pip
pip-0d69d96acf26.text: Lovely. I'd call it personal, but it never is.

pip-caddbf37aa93.speaker: pip
pip-caddbf37aa93.text: Ow. Noted. Adding it to the list.

pip-664e103a9394.speaker: pip
pip-664e103a9394.text: Oi! That was my good side. I have one.

pip-5627e009c340.speaker: pip
pip-5627e009c340.text: I'm fine. It's a flesh wound and a moral failing.

pip-13f1c77acce9.speaker: pip
pip-13f1c77acce9.text: Not dying today. I have an appointment.

pip-1bf0035108d2.speaker: pip
pip-1bf0035108d2.text: Get up. You don't get to die before I get my revenge. Wait, that's my line.

pip-27e6679bc04f.speaker: pip
pip-27e6679bc04f.text: Hey. Hey! Stay with us. I've buried enough friends.

pip-9e124b7c7fa0.speaker: pip
pip-9e124b7c7fa0.text: Money. The only friend who never sold me out.

pip-8ba21e43d259.speaker: pip
pip-8ba21e43d259.text: Shiny. Mine. Ours. Fine, ours, but I'm holding it.

pip-9e2da84f8856.speaker: pip
pip-9e2da84f8856.text: Down we go. Every step is closer to a conversation I've rehearsed for three years.

pip-996f5367944a.speaker: pip
pip-996f5367944a.text: Stairs. Of course. Nothing good ever lives upstairs.

pip-f1f730dd2e7e.speaker: pip
pip-f1f730dd2e7e.text: I'll take first watch. I don't sleep much anyway.

pip-833ee2073aae.speaker: pip
pip-833ee2073aae.text: Wake me if anything dies. Or if anything's about to.

pip-13fccd41bb1d.speaker: pip
pip-13fccd41bb1d.text: Ow. Whoever built this, I'd love to shake their hand. Slowly. Around the neck.

pip-4496143a5117.speaker: pip
pip-4496143a5117.text: Told you. I'm a delight in a crisis.

pip-8311c2535bfb.speaker: pip
pip-8311c2535bfb.text: That's that. Anyone have a list of who's next?

pip-d09b9f30a55b.speaker: pip
pip-d09b9f30a55b.text: Sharper, faster, angrier. A balanced diet.

pip-87c1dbdbc5f5.speaker: pip
pip-87c1dbdbc5f5.text: A hidden door. I love hidden doors. They never pretend to be anything else.

pip-9a699bc90364.speaker: pip
pip-9a699bc90364.text: I'll check the corners. People hide things there. I used to.

pip-2f939ce3c4d9.speaker: pip
pip-2f939ce3c4d9.text: New room. Same old tower. Same old liars.

nettle-580f66c971e9.speaker: nettle
nettle-580f66c971e9.text: Easy. I once fought a hundred of these with a teapot.

fizzwick-c905d382a112.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-c905d382a112.text: Pip, Fizzwick has noticed you never sleep. Fizzwick finds this suspicious, and quietly admirable.

pip-9c95a8758825.speaker: pip
pip-9c95a8758825.text: Lantern Row Crew. Eleven of us. Best pockets in Emberhollow. We never robbed anybody who couldn't afford it. Mostly.

pip-2f4b258ef956.speaker: pip
pip-2f4b258ef956.text: Do you know the worst part of being betrayed? It isn't the betrayal. It's that I admired his handwriting.

pip-045b7198a090.speaker: pip
pip-045b7198a090.text: Brambur keeps apologising to the monsters. I keep not apologising to anyone. We balance out.

pip-1b6384aac256.speaker: pip
pip-1b6384aac256.text: Fizzwick talks about himself in the third person. I talk about everyone else in the past tense. We're both coping.

pip-6704a2ce9631.speaker: pip
pip-6704a2ce9631.text: My sister used to say revenge is a dish best served warm, because cold food gives you indigestion. She was seven. She was right.

grumsh-3f34f9af02c2.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-3f34f9af02c2.text: Pip does not speak of what was lost. I know that silence. I have written four hundred lines about the same one.

nettle-77a3c362d325.speaker: nettle
nettle-77a3c362d325.text: I was married to a queen for a week. It ended over a disagreement about a throne. Hers. It was a very good throne.

narrator-25632f14406a.speaker: narrator
narrator-25632f14406a.text: Behind a heap of gnawed barrels, someone has chalked a lantern with four rays on the stone. The chalk is old. The dust around it is not.

narrator-e0e0655aa0ef.speaker: narrator
narrator-e0e0655aa0ef.text: A halfling thieves' mark, the kind guild runners leave to say a place is safe. Someone down here knew the code.

narrator-51851889e10f.speaker: narrator
narrator-51851889e10f.text: A loose stone. Behind it, a folded cult payment slip. Forty sovereigns, paid to G. Vane, for the Row.

narrator-14d623fb0ef3.speaker: narrator
narrator-14d623fb0ef3.text: Somebody named G. Vane was paid forty sovereigns for something called the Row. Whatever that is, it sounds like a sale.

narrator-c2d604ec1566.speaker: narrator
narrator-c2d604ec1566.text: You find a stone that moves, and a slip of paper that dissolves at a touch. Three words survive: paid to G. Vane.

narrator-990027a1c0be.speaker: narrator
narrator-990027a1c0be.text: Half sunk in the shallows lies a child's rowboat, painted with the lantern mark. The name on the stern is nearly gone: P, O, S, Y.

narrator-bca2672c2798.speaker: narrator
narrator-bca2672c2798.text: A child's boat, painted with a thief's mark and a girl's name. Somebody small once loved it.

narrator-b3faeaee8235.speaker: narrator
narrator-b3faeaee8235.text: Boot prints, deep, from a robed figure carrying something small. They lead to a landing, and a ledger page stuck in the mud: tithe received, one halfling girl, unharmed, for the Seneschal's own.

narrator-45d17876558d.speaker: narrator
narrator-45d17876558d.text: A tithe slip. One halfling girl, unharmed, for the Seneschal's own. The cult took a living child.

narrator-b9ac73176901.speaker: narrator
narrator-b9ac73176901.text: The mud has swallowed whatever there was to find. You manage only a scrap of blue ribbon, caught on the oar.

narrator-41e4446c22db.speaker: narrator
narrator-41e4446c22db.text: A wall of green crystal, scratched with a cult cipher. A column of names and numbers. One line is underlined twice.

narrator-4e466436d711.speaker: narrator
narrator-4e466436d711.text: The cipher unravels. Seneschal of Keys, Garrick Vane, keeper of every door in the vault. And below it: Posy T. held in the servants' ward, to be returned when the Row is quiet.

narrator-de2430cd7a50.speaker: narrator
narrator-de2430cd7a50.text: The cipher fights you. You catch a title, Seneschal, and a name, Vane, before the rest swims away.

narrator-3bd3c9f9b41a.speaker: narrator
narrator-3bd3c9f9b41a.text: At a cold forge, a Lantern Row key lies half finished in a clay mould, beside a note on cult stationery. Hurry the keys. The Sovereign's patience is thin, and so is mine. G.V.

narrator-d8f02755afd4.speaker: narrator
narrator-d8f02755afd4.text: Quick fingers, soft wax. When you lift your hand, the cast is perfect, and no one is the wiser. In the bow of the key, a pair of initials.

narrator-215c805f7935.speaker: narrator
narrator-215c805f7935.text: The wax cracks, the mould shatters, and the key stays where it was. You pocket the note instead.

narrator-421cecec7bf2.speaker: narrator
narrator-421cecec7bf2.text: Near the vault stair, a lantern hangs in an alcove, still burning. A Lantern Row lamp. Eleven notches are cut into the iron, one for each of the Crew.

narrator-95c6943bd4a0.speaker: narrator
narrator-95c6943bd4a0.text: Beyond the alcove stands a brass door worked with lanterns. The Seneschal's counting room, you think. It will open for anyone who is not afraid of what is behind it.

narrator-ef0881b36d3d.speaker: narrator
narrator-ef0881b36d3d.text: You light the lantern again, and carry the flame to the brass door.

narrator-06f142bdb0d7.speaker: narrator
narrator-06f142bdb0d7.text: A brass door worked with lantern marks, and a keyhole built for small hands. Some quarrels are not yours to settle alone. Pip belongs here, and Pip is not with you.

narrator-041aeb5bef90.speaker: narrator
narrator-041aeb5bef90.text: A brass door worked with lantern marks. A whole story is written on it, and you have missed the first pages. Look for Lantern Row marks on the floors above.

narrator-fbc5b63dae33.speaker: narrator
narrator-fbc5b63dae33.text: Gold light from a brazier. Ledgers stacked to the rafters. A man in a grey coat, with a ring of keys at his belt as long as your arm, writes without looking up.

narrator-862aa919cdb3.speaker: narrator
narrator-862aa919cdb3.text: Pip's hand is on a knife. Garrick's hands are open on the desk. Behind you, the door has swung shut on its own. Roll if you want answers, and know the whole table is watching.

narrator-26dfac0d10c8.speaker: narrator
narrator-26dfac0d10c8.text: You watch his hands, not his face. A tremor in his left thumb, the thing he always did when he would rather not say. He is not lying about the fire. He is lying by leaving something out.

narrator-6e51eb95225e.speaker: narrator
narrator-6e51eb95225e.text: He is very good. Every line lands calm, every pause is rehearsed. Whatever lies beneath it, you cannot find it.

narrator-58bdf9d1c9f4.speaker: narrator
narrator-58bdf9d1c9f4.text: You set the cast down: a Lantern Row key, newly forged, with Garrick's own initials in the bow. He looks at it the way a man looks at his own gravestone.

narrator-a743ed80e157.speaker: narrator
narrator-a743ed80e157.text: There are no more questions. The guards are gone, the keys lie on the desk, and a knife is in Pip's hand. Everyone at the table is looking at you.

narrator-62aa3410c461.speaker: narrator
narrator-62aa3410c461.text: Vengeance or mercy. There is no die for this one.

narrator-4c05cc14a6f3.speaker: narrator
narrator-4c05cc14a6f3.text: You nod, and say nothing. Pip does not say a word either. It is quick, and cleaner than Garrick deserved.

narrator-2b490b8ec404.speaker: narrator
narrator-2b490b8ec404.text: He does not finish the sentence. The keys hit the floor, and the whole ring rings like a bell.

narrator-841acaf57eeb.speaker: narrator
narrator-841acaf57eeb.text: Garrick said Posy was alive, and the only man who knew where is on the floor. The strongbox holds three hundred gold, a ledger of every name the Row ever sold, and a plain dagger forged from a Lantern Row lamp.

narrator-d63b79e6a455.speaker: narrator
narrator-d63b79e6a455.text: The strongbox holds three hundred gold, a ledger of every name the Row ever sold, and a plain dagger forged from a Lantern Row lamp.

narrator-379bdf428968.speaker: narrator
narrator-379bdf428968.text: You say stop. Pip hears you, and does not stop. It is quick, and nobody in the room says a word afterwards.

narrator-d9ae928f83c8.speaker: narrator
narrator-d9ae928f83c8.text: Put it down, you say, and for a long moment, nothing. Then the knife trembles, and drops point first into the desk, quivering.

narrator-abc271af39b9.speaker: narrator
narrator-abc271af39b9.text: Garrick goes in chains. Pip does not look at him once. The whole way back up the stair, Pip does not say a word.

narrator-1c8ceef68269.speaker: narrator
narrator-1c8ceef68269.text: Fenn and Daughters, Pawnbrokers, sits crooked between the smithy and the temple. The shutters are closed at noon, which is unheard of. A bell jangles as you enter.

narrator-3ce80b89f53a.speaker: narrator
narrator-3ce80b89f53a.text: Odalys slides three things across the counter: a forged ticket, a smear of grave dirt on a handkerchief, and a candle stub that smells of lilies. Where you start is up to you.

narrator-25f60c820e09.speaker: narrator
narrator-25f60c820e09.text: Three threads, one forger. Pull them in any order. Roll well, and the town starts to talk.

narrator-a1ac06c0d4c6.speaker: narrator
narrator-a1ac06c0d4c6.text: The ink is Odalys's, but the loops are wrong. The forger is left handed and smudged every final letter. The paper smells faintly of lilies and damp earth.

narrator-c62bfffc8703.speaker: narrator
narrator-c62bfffc8703.text: You squint until the loops swim. A forgery, certainly, but the ink gives nothing else away. Odalys wrings her hands.

narrator-a064c54cc6b8.speaker: narrator
narrator-a064c54cc6b8.text: The night watchman eyes your coin, then your face, then talks. A stooped figure with a spade and a lantern has crossed Cant Street after the third bell, three nights running, always toward the pawnshop.

narrator-d9306b132a69.speaker: narrator
narrator-d9306b132a69.text: The watchman clams up. Questions about grave dirt make him nervous, and he suggests you take them elsewhere. A round of drinks might have helped. It costs you ten gold anyway.

narrator-7090220c2fa6.speaker: narrator
narrator-7090220c2fa6.text: Crouched behind a rain barrel, you wait. After the bell, a stooped man with a spade slips a candlestick through the pawnshop's coal hatch, whistling a hymn off key. Dirt crumbles from his boots. He never sees you.

narrator-ca5877602362.speaker: narrator
narrator-ca5877602362.text: Your knee cracks like a dry twig. A shape in the alley freezes, then bolts, leaving behind the smell of lilies and nothing more.

narrator-222fc6a1c1d6.speaker: narrator
narrator-222fc6a1c1d6.text: Odalys has found her nerve, and a lantern. Everyone in the shop is waiting for a name. Three people could have done this. Choose carefully, and know that a wrong name costs her dearly.

narrator-70ecf2fa66a9.speaker: narrator
narrator-70ecf2fa66a9.text: Your suspect proves their innocence quickly, loudly, and in front of witnesses. Odalys apologises to everyone and pays for the trouble. It stings her purse, and her pride.

narrator-9c6446d73c6f.speaker: narrator
narrator-9c6446d73c6f.text: You find Tuck Harrow in the churchyard at dusk, leaning on his spade, a lantern at his feet. Dirt on his boots. Lilies on his hat.

narrator-f7a55661eeb5.speaker: narrator
narrator-f7a55661eeb5.text: You lay the evidence out on a headstone. His smile fades. He sits down hard on a grave.

narrator-a1f230d026d9.speaker: narrator
narrator-a1f230d026d9.text: Odalys, at your elbow, has gone very pale. The choice, and the consequence, are yours.

narrator-4765d5c3882f.speaker: narrator
narrator-4765d5c3882f.text: Captain Rowan's men come at dawn. Tuck goes quietly, and the town sleeps easier, though a gravedigger's wife weeps on Cant Street all that week.

narrator-305e770fe080.speaker: narrator
narrator-305e770fe080.text: The town never learns. Odalys sleeps well, and Tuck's wife is soon sitting up in bed, thanks to a physician Odalys quietly pays.

narrator-9f3300a7785d.speaker: narrator
narrator-9f3300a7785d.text: Tuck bolts over the churchyard wall and is gone before you can blink. Odalys sits among the graves and laughs, a short, tired laugh.

narrator-61ac65453426.speaker: narrator
narrator-61ac65453426.text: You name a price for your silence, and Tuck pays it in coin he cannot spare.

narrator-3eff080cd250.speaker: narrator
narrator-3eff080cd250.text: Odalys is trembling. Tuck is waiting, and so is the night.

narrator-6ed4ebf207c0.speaker: narrator
narrator-6ed4ebf207c0.text: Harl Tollow mends nets on the Emberhollow wharf, though no boat has gone out in a month. He does not look up until your shadow falls across the cord.

narrator-e6c9027e00b2.speaker: narrator
narrator-e6c9027e00b2.text: Harl presses his wife's silver brooch into your palm. It is cold as pond water. So you know them, he says, and so they know you.

narrator-8886e3890f16.speaker: narrator
narrator-8886e3890f16.text: He weeps without embarrassment, and hums a few bars of the Evening Hymn, badly.

narrator-521fc936bc64.speaker: narrator
narrator-521fc936bc64.text: Harl hears you out with his hands folded around the net cord. He does not weep. That is worse.

narrator-0d2f7b194745.speaker: narrator
narrator-0d2f7b194745.text: A stair of slick stone leads to a half drowned chapel. Fourteen benches stand in the black water. A hymnal lies open on a lectern, its pages swollen but still legible. Somewhere beneath the floor, a woman is humming.

narrator-1651e6e3bdd0.speaker: narrator
narrator-1651e6e3bdd0.text: A clever party rolls before it touches anything.

narrator-395bc4fb9cf8.speaker: narrator
narrator-395bc4fb9cf8.text: The last verse is in a different hand, written in haste. Sing me out, if you love me. The deep wants a choir, and we are all the choir it will get. It is a binding rite. Sung backwards, it would also release.

narrator-2955edcedc44.speaker: narrator
narrator-2955edcedc44.text: The ink has run into a blue bruise. You catch a word here and there: sing, deep, hold. Enough to be afraid, not enough to be useful.

narrator-95c54f3f92e5.speaker: narrator
narrator-95c54f3f92e5.text: The humming does not come from the water. It comes from the lectern's brass bell, and when you lean close, a voice speaks from it.

narrator-b37c5a2950d2.speaker: narrator
narrator-b37c5a2950d2.text: The humming slides away from you like a fish. You hear only the water lapping at fourteen empty benches.

narrator-ab4c18272ee6.speaker: narrator
narrator-ab4c18272ee6.text: You close the hymnal gently. Beyond the chapel, a passage slopes down toward cold, black water.

narrator-2ec5e9c51576.speaker: narrator
narrator-2ec5e9c51576.text: A black pool, perfectly still, ringed by fourteen stone posts. Something sings beneath it. You decide you are not ready. The chapel might have answers.

narrator-30aa1c718dca.speaker: narrator
narrator-30aa1c718dca.text: Fourteen shapes hang in the water below you, robed and swaying. Their mouths open and close in the Evening Hymn. In the middle, tied to a rotted post, a bell as wide as a cartwheel rings without a clapper. A woman's face drifts nearest the surface.

narrator-4422fb820018.speaker: narrator
narrator-4422fb820018.text: You may free them, or you may take the Choir for yourselves. Either way, the bell needs a hand on it, and the water does not like that.

narrator-4b31fcb21298.speaker: narrator
narrator-4b31fcb21298.text: The water surges and drags at your ankles. Cold bites to the bone. Everyone takes six damage before the Pool lets go.

narrator-b3363142d570.speaker: narrator
narrator-b3363142d570.text: You sing the last verse backwards, one note at a time. The bell rings once, a clean, ordinary sound, and stops. Fourteen lights rise from the water like lanterns, and one of them lingers at your shoulder.

narrator-1e5bdd1500ce.speaker: narrator
narrator-1e5bdd1500ce.text: The Pool is only water now. The way is clear.

narrator-c4395a191b48.speaker: narrator
narrator-c4395a191b48.text: You take up the Choir's thread and pull it taut. Fourteen faces turn toward you, empty and obedient. The bell speaks in a voice like cold iron, and it is yours.

narrator-48b1fa9c3036.speaker: narrator
narrator-48b1fa9c3036.text: She does not stop singing. The Sisters will fight for you, now, wherever there is water to fight in. Whether they would have wished it is another question. The bell's iron heart drops into your hands.

narrator-0f846a5cf1ab.speaker: narrator
narrator-0f846a5cf1ab.text: In a seam of green crystal, a woman in a scorched leather apron sits with her knees drawn up and a hammer in her fist. She flinches at your torch, then lowers the hammer an inch.

narrator-df15ee3923cc.speaker: narrator
narrator-df15ee3923cc.text: Her eyes flick to the crystal over your shoulder. In it, faint and wrong, your party's reflection looks back, one beat late.

narrator-c9b0795267af.speaker: narrator
narrator-c9b0795267af.text: She will not believe you, not until you leave a flask of water and twenty gold at her feet. That seems to do it.

narrator-2e1a9dc0ab8d.speaker: narrator
narrator-2e1a9dc0ab8d.text: The kiln is a brick cavern, warm for the first time in a week. In the middle stands the Mirror, tall as a door, framed in black iron. The glass shows the room as it will be in an hour: your party, exactly where you stand, and your faces, tired.

narrator-2a9d33c14db5.speaker: narrator
narrator-2a9d33c14db5.text: It wants something from you. Mirrors always do.

narrator-be3deeba357f.speaker: narrator
narrator-be3deeba357f.text: You trace the iron frame with a steady finger. Ten runes, each ending in an eye. It sees what we see, you realise, and reports it to the vault below. Break it and the Sovereign loses an eye. Gaze long enough, and you will see through it. You will also be seen.

narrator-5ce9d6917b31.speaker: narrator
narrator-5ce9d6917b31.text: Your reflection grabs your wrist, cold as a river stone, and lets go. Everyone takes four damage from the cold.

narrator-55dcf593769d.speaker: narrator
narrator-55dcf593769d.text: The hammer rebounds as if from a drum. Shock shivers up your arm. Everyone takes five damage as the Mirror laughs, soundlessly.

narrator-1947ae43abdb.speaker: narrator
narrator-1947ae43abdb.text: The hammer comes down. The Mirror does not break so much as sigh. Ten eyes go dark, one by one, and a thousand silver shards rain across the kiln floor. Far beneath the vault, something large snarls, and cannot say why.

narrator-2bd53f80109b.speaker: narrator
narrator-2bd53f80109b.text: You look. The glass ripples, then clears. A long table lit by violet fire. A crown of black iron. A staff with a crack beneath the third ring. And then the Sovereign turns his head, and looks straight back at you.

narrator-a7d41f6e8c9e.speaker: narrator
narrator-a7d41f6e8c9e.text: The glass goes dark. You know where to strike the staff. He knows your faces. Somewhere above, a seal cracks, and you glimpse the cache of the Glassworks guild, three hundred gold left behind.

narrator-d71369563eb1.speaker: narrator
narrator-d71369563eb1.text: She laughs, a little wildly, and sets down her hammer for the first time in months.

narrator-2fa93d4c61c9.speaker: narrator
narrator-2fa93d4c61c9.text: In the cold ash of a collapsed barracks, a pale man in a Warden's tabard stands at attention before a wall of scratched names. He does not blink. Frost forms on your armour as you approach.

narrator-033e0fed655a.speaker: narrator
narrator-033e0fed655a.text: He says why the seals fell on my watch too quickly, the way a man says a thing he has said to himself a thousand times. Whatever happened, the Sergeant suspects someone he loved.

narrator-4cffa8ad82a1.speaker: narrator
narrator-4cffa8ad82a1.text: His face gives you nothing, not even breath. A man long dead keeps his secrets well.

narrator-ca1d16e789e0.speaker: narrator
narrator-ca1d16e789e0.text: Deep in the vault, the Watch's barracks has survived untouched: a ring of bunks and a wall of names. Three tags hang on three rusted nails. Each has a story, and each is worth a roll.

narrator-7dee94a45f6c.speaker: narrator
narrator-7dee94a45f6c.text: Her bunk is neat. A letter lies under the pillow. Dunstan told me to guard the north seal. He said the Sergeant ordered it. The Sergeant never did.

narrator-72cb7c74fec2.speaker: narrator
narrator-72cb7c74fec2.text: A neat bunk, a folded blanket, dust. Whatever Ilsa Marn left behind, she left it somewhere else.

narrator-82036a4b92a6.speaker: narrator
narrator-82036a4b92a6.text: Joss Kettering died of a blade in the back, not the front. The sheath on his belt carries Dunstan's initials.

narrator-38b88ec8b6d9.speaker: narrator
narrator-38b88ec8b6d9.text: The tags are brittle and the bones beneath are long past telling stories. Whatever killed him, you cannot say.

narrator-9d323cb9eed9.speaker: narrator
narrator-9d323cb9eed9.text: The lock gives. Inside, a ledger of seal rotas in Dunstan's hand, and a purse of Sovereign's gold, minted before Malthrax ever rose.

narrator-cd3a2d22c2d5.speaker: narrator
narrator-cd3a2d22c2d5.text: The lock jams, and a needle springs from the hasp. Everyone takes four damage as the poison burns off.

narrator-6f5a0ff942cd.speaker: narrator
narrator-6f5a0ff942cd.text: You gather what you have found. Behind you, the frost on the wall begins to creep.

narrator-0accf9a2cf04.speaker: narrator
narrator-0accf9a2cf04.text: Frost pools around a rusted gate. Someone is waiting beyond it, but you are not ready. The Fourth Company's barracks should have answers.

narrator-480d0f9192f0.speaker: narrator
narrator-480d0f9192f0.text: Sergeant Crane's ghost waits on a landing of black stone, his tabard bright with frost. The names on the wall behind you seem to be listening.

narrator-bc671b9e1c5d.speaker: narrator
narrator-bc671b9e1c5d.text: The evidence in your hands is plain: Dunstan Hale opened the north seal for Sovereign's gold, and Joss Kettering died trying to stop him.

narrator-3c60eca2c9a9.speaker: narrator
narrator-3c60eca2c9a9.text: You have only fragments. Not proof. The Sergeant will know the difference.

narrator-96bd5750ae9b.speaker: narrator
narrator-96bd5750ae9b.text: The cold bites. Everyone takes five damage.

narrator-c1e97fa791a9.speaker: narrator
narrator-c1e97fa791a9.text: You tell it plainly. Dunstan's gold. Joss's back. Ilsa's letter. The ghost listens without moving, until the frost on his tabard cracks like glass.

narrator-894a5fff1ef6.speaker: narrator
narrator-894a5fff1ef6.text: He draws a sword of pale light and turns toward the depths. His tabard glows, the Watch's colours, bright as dawn.

narrator-7720d4cc25aa.speaker: narrator
narrator-7720d4cc25aa.text: He held the line, you say. To the last. The Sergeant closes his eyes.

narrator-11be44203d35.speaker: narrator
narrator-11be44203d35.text: The frost melts. Crane salutes you, and the salute is the last thing you see before he is simply gone. On the step, he has left a pouch of old coin, and two vials. A debt, paid forward.

pip-631c76c65607.speaker: pip
pip-631c76c65607.text: Nice room. Plenty of places to hide a knife.

pip-d4fd4100a161.speaker: pip
pip-d4fd4100a161.text: Quiet. I hate quiet. Quiet is when people are planning something.

pip-a9bc0979614b.speaker: pip
pip-a9bc0979614b.text: Good bones. Terrible company, I assume.

pip-6cf226ced559.speaker: pip
pip-6cf226ced559.text: Coin. Warm, reliable, never asks questions.

pip-15542909a199.speaker: pip
pip-15542909a199.text: Take it. Everything in a place like this was stolen from someone anyway.

pip-181170b4ee88.speaker: pip
pip-181170b4ee88.text: A hidden door. The only honest thing in this tower.

pip-d20228ea474d.speaker: pip
pip-d20228ea474d.text: Ha. Called it. Quietly. In my head. Every time.

pip-1b89ec6422fc.speaker: pip
pip-1b89ec6422fc.text: That one is big. Good. I am in a mood.

pip-8998fc7886c6.speaker: pip
pip-8998fc7886c6.text: I'll go around the back. It's where I do my best work.

pip-efbdd75ee31d.speaker: pip
pip-efbdd75ee31d.text: No. Not you too. I have done this before and I hated it.

pip-a79f06189695.speaker: pip
pip-a79f06189695.text: Emberhollow. Smells like bread, smoke and old lies. Home.

pip-88d4d24b317e.speaker: pip
pip-88d4d24b317e.text: Take a good look at it. Somebody in this town is still hiding something.

pip-67b006135e88.speaker: pip
pip-67b006135e88.text: Lantern Row Crew. Eleven of us, every one a thief. We never robbed anyone who couldn't spare it.

pip-16bba8d89e48.speaker: pip
pip-16bba8d89e48.text: Three years ago it was eleven. Now it is me. I'll tell you why when I'm ready, or drunk.

pip-37620f1dc4a6.speaker: pip
pip-37620f1dc4a6.text: My sister Posy was seven when she learned to pick a lock. She picked mine. I'd locked her out for being too loud.

pip-111bbf0bc055.speaker: pip
pip-111bbf0bc055.text: She's the reason I am still down here. Do not make it a thing.

pip-64248d2b8c85.speaker: pip
pip-64248d2b8c85.text: My partner was Garrick Vane. He taught me to open any lock with a hairpin and any person with a smile.

pip-26229a64f5b9.speaker: pip
pip-26229a64f5b9.text: Both lessons have since been used on me. Excellent teacher.

pip-6e5c131aa1d3.speaker: pip
pip-6e5c131aa1d3.text: The night the Row burned, I smelled lamp oil before I smelled smoke. Somebody poured it. Somebody had a key.

pip-8908ed179981.speaker: pip
pip-8908ed179981.text: I have replayed that night ten thousand times. It always ends with Garrick, smiling.

pip-ddff7f1fc8b0.speaker: pip
pip-ddff7f1fc8b0.text: When we find him, let me talk first. After that, you can have your turn, if there is anything left.

pip-90bda7ed3cd8.speaker: pip
pip-90bda7ed3cd8.text: If I get this wrong, tell Posy I was funny. I would like to be remembered as funny.

pip-f0ec6279038c.speaker: pip
pip-f0ec6279038c.text: Not Brambur. Not like this. Somebody get a healer. Somebody get me a healer, my hands are shaking.

pip-ba0436896984.speaker: pip
pip-ba0436896984.text: Not Fizzwick. Not like this. Somebody get a healer. Somebody get me a healer, my hands are shaking.

pip-88f5e7b655b1.speaker: pip
pip-88f5e7b655b1.text: Not Grumsh. Not like this. Somebody get a healer. Somebody get me a healer, my hands are shaking.

pip-f18cd8467439.speaker: pip
pip-f18cd8467439.text: Not Zizzy. Not like this. Somebody get a healer. Somebody get me a healer, my hands are shaking.

pip-04cdb547a751.speaker: pip
pip-04cdb547a751.text: Not Vexrath. Not like this. Somebody get a healer. Somebody get me a healer, my hands are shaking.

pip-fc8577c30da2.speaker: pip
pip-fc8577c30da2.text: Not Nettle. Not like this. Somebody get a healer. Somebody get me a healer, my hands are shaking.

pip-8a9244e148b6.speaker: pip
pip-8a9244e148b6.text: Not Liora. Not like this. Somebody get a healer. Somebody get me a healer, my hands are shaking.

pip-0df03c2c22e4.speaker: pip
pip-0df03c2c22e4.text: Not Ser Aldric. Not like this. Somebody get a healer. Somebody get me a healer, my hands are shaking.

pip-02ea1722dcd7.speaker: pip
pip-02ea1722dcd7.text: Lovely party. Everyone smiling. I never trust a room where everyone is smiling.

pip-43a918c14f8b.speaker: pip
pip-43a918c14f8b.text: He took the Princess. Fine. I have been waiting years for a reason to go down there.

narrator-890816b987f2.speaker: narrator
narrator-890816b987f2.text: Back in Emberhollow, in the Boar & Spoon, which still smells faintly of smoke, Elowen draws Dawnfang and lays it on your shoulder.

pip-c7dd063520df.speaker: pip
pip-c7dd063520df.text: Malthrax is down. Garrick is still out there somewhere. Do not look so worried. I am patient.

narrator-39c12350b369.speaker: narrator
narrator-39c12350b369.text: A note: "Lantern Row was here. Do not follow. Not sorry."

narrator-f45e1ef5e9d7.speaker: narrator
narrator-f45e1ef5e9d7.text: Dozens of tiny shrines line this room: thimbles, buttons and bent nails arranged with real devotion around a portrait of a very fat rat.

pip-e78704b9f237.speaker: pip
pip-e78704b9f237.text: I would say I forgive him. I would be lying. I am just tired of carrying it.

narrator-0a9fa15354d1.speaker: narrator
narrator-0a9fa15354d1.text: At a corner table of the Boar & Spoon, a small halfling girl with a scorched blue ribbon pretends she has not been crying. Pip crosses the whole room without a word, and then says several.

pip-2f332c346522.speaker: pip
pip-2f332c346522.text: Garrick is dead, and the Row is paid. I thought I would feel lighter. Ask me again in a year.

narrator-00762f4b7195.speaker: narrator
narrator-00762f4b7195.text: That night, Pip hangs a lantern in the window of the Boar & Spoon. It burns for the eleven of the Row, and for one more, Pip hopes.

maelis-31b09d97b333.speaker: maelis
