maelis-31b09d97b333.text: Mind the roots. They remember everyone who walks on them. I am Maelis Dewbough, keeper of this orchard, which is a grand title for the last gardener alive.

maelis-94cd382a1365.speaker: maelis
maelis-94cd382a1365.text: The roof fell and the sky came in, and I thought it a mercy. Then the fruit turned grey. The trees are dying, and the old gate to the north will not wake. It is the Gate of the Silver Court. It should open at moonrise and water the whole orchard with light. It has not done so in sixty years.

maelis-670ea2536dc1.speaker: maelis
maelis-670ea2536dc1.text: Read the trees. Read the sky. Read the gate. Three answers to one question: what is killing my orchard? Do that, and the Silverfruit are yours, what is left of them.

maelis-50a3d7bea6b0.speaker: maelis
maelis-50a3d7bea6b0.text: Men came with barrels, the winter the roof fell. They said they were mending the gate. They went in loud and came out quiet. Look for their boots.

maelis-4129ded47b0c.speaker: maelis
maelis-4129ded47b0c.text: Then go. The trees are all around you, the gate is at the north edge, and the sky is wherever you stand. Come back and tell me what you find.

maelis-e0affe733924.speaker: maelis
maelis-e0affe733924.text: Still here, and so are my trees. Trees, sky, gate. In any order, but the gate will not listen until you have read both the trees and the sky.

maelis-d7b97ed6fcc6.speaker: maelis
maelis-d7b97ed6fcc6.text: The gate has changed its voice. I can feel it in my teeth. Whatever you did there, the old roots under it are awake. Go down to them. Tell me what they say.

aelindra-05bf01bf3987.speaker: aelindra
aelindra-05bf01bf3987.text: You sang me awake. It has been sixty years. I thought the sky had forgotten us.

aelindra-c0bb42f9d9d9.speaker: aelindra
aelindra-c0bb42f9d9d9.text: You broke my door and woke me with a splinter in my side. I am old, and I am angry, and I am listening.

aelindra-83c46b2f09cc.speaker: aelindra
aelindra-83c46b2f09cc.text: The salt smells of men with keys. You turned a key I did not choose. Still, you are here, and they are not.

aelindra-7830ff714ea9.speaker: aelindra
aelindra-7830ff714ea9.text: I am Aelindra, the Heartroot of the Silver Court. The salt has gone to my heart. A little care will save me, and a little greed will end me. Choose.

aelindra-af04b739897e.speaker: aelindra
aelindra-af04b739897e.text: A boon is for those who ask without wanting. You want very loudly.

aelindra-bfc3acbde5f9.speaker: aelindra
aelindra-bfc3acbde5f9.text: There. That is what rain is for. Go and tell Maelis the orchard will blossom at the next moonrise.

aelindra-1804c6960ed5.speaker: aelindra
aelindra-1804c6960ed5.text: A gift, and no more than a gift. The orchard will be slow to forgive. Tell Maelis what you were given.

aelindra-f9605806432a.speaker: aelindra
aelindra-f9605806432a.text: Take it, then. Take it and go. Do not come back in spring.

maelis-ab42cbcffe27.speaker: maelis
maelis-ab42cbcffe27.text: You did it. Sixty years, and the orchard remembers its own name. I cannot pay you enough, so I will pay you with what grows here.

maelis-c833e64cae35.speaker: maelis
maelis-c833e64cae35.text: The gate was a door, you know. Not a wall. It will open for you again, whenever the moon is out and you need somewhere to be quiet.

maelis-dc1fa7f3d6f7.speaker: maelis
maelis-dc1fa7f3d6f7.text: I could feel it when you cut. The roots told me before you came up the stair. You took what was growing, and you left what was dying.

maelis-1225e18f6598.speaker: maelis
maelis-1225e18f6598.text: I will not take it from you. That is not the keeper's way. But I will not thank you, either. Here. A little coin, for the road. You will not be welcome in the spring.

maelis-086998365787.speaker: maelis
maelis-086998365787.text: She gave you that? She has not given a fruit in sixty years. Then it is a good sign. Slow, but good. The salt will take a season to leave.

maelis-1fd8fbc0d064.speaker: maelis
maelis-1fd8fbc0d064.text: Take this wreath, with my thanks. It was my mother's. May it keep a few of your heads cool.

maelis-5aa65e85474a.speaker: maelis
maelis-5aa65e85474a.text: The orchard is doing what orchards do. Go on. I am busy being right about the weather.

narrator-9fadb059e3a2.speaker: narrator
narrator-9fadb059e3a2.text: Where the cavern roof gave way, the sky pours in. A hundred pale trees lean in the wet grass, their silver leaves gone the colour of ash. Under the oldest sits an elf woman with moss on her shoulders, pruning a branch that is no longer there.

narrator-3874437cd41b.speaker: narrator
narrator-3874437cd41b.text: Rain ticks on the leaves and runs down the trunks in thin white streaks.

narrator-9b16edf13c45.speaker: narrator
narrator-9b16edf13c45.text: A low mist threads between the trunks, and it clings to the bark like breath on glass.

narrator-dcf8b3bf2080.speaker: narrator
narrator-dcf8b3bf2080.text: The sky above the hole is full of stars, and the healthy trees glow faintly under them. The sick ones are only black shapes.

narrator-f5a86c4a70f1.speaker: narrator
narrator-f5a86c4a70f1.text: Her hands stop moving. She does not look at you.

narrator-dbbc6010f95c.speaker: narrator
narrator-dbbc6010f95c.text: Her face is bark and patience. Whatever she is holding back stays held.

narrator-abf7f3962156.speaker: narrator
narrator-abf7f3962156.text: You have not yet read the trees.

narrator-18d553290135.speaker: narrator
narrator-18d553290135.text: You have not yet read the open sky.

narrator-c7eade2be97b.speaker: narrator
narrator-c7eade2be97b.text: The trees have told you what they know.

narrator-bf1c28e9b3d8.speaker: narrator
narrator-bf1c28e9b3d8.text: The sky has told you what it knows.

narrator-17d2598829cd.speaker: narrator
narrator-17d2598829cd.text: Pale bark and ash coloured leaves. Fruit hangs in hard grey knots, and each one holds a faint smear of old light, like a coin seen through water.

narrator-a0ec4b74b83f.speaker: narrator
narrator-a0ec4b74b83f.text: Rain runs down the trunks in white streaks, and where it runs whitest, something crusted is washing out of the bark.

narrator-fbed0ebabbbb.speaker: narrator
narrator-fbed0ebabbbb.text: Mist beads on the bark in strange hard drops, as if it were settling on salt.

narrator-297eef03405d.speaker: narrator
narrator-297eef03405d.text: In the dark, the living trees glow silver and the dying ones swallow the light. Count the black ones. There are too many.

narrator-ff4fcf04bb54.speaker: narrator
narrator-ff4fcf04bb54.text: The roots are laced with a white crust. Brine. Cult brine, poured into the soil by the barrelful. Salt to kill the roots, so the gate would starve and stay shut.

narrator-9285880d2842.speaker: narrator
narrator-9285880d2842.text: The bark is only bark. Whatever is wrong is down in the soil, and the soil keeps its own counsel.

narrator-44cc8b2e6c2f.speaker: narrator
narrator-44cc8b2e6c2f.text: Boot prints, heavy ones, in a line: men carrying barrels. They go to the gate and come back empty. One left boot is missing a heel nail, and the nail lies in the grass, bright as a tooth. You pocket it.

narrator-026dcff44366.speaker: narrator
narrator-026dcff44366.text: The grass holds a hundred prints and says nothing. A crow watches you from a branch, unimpressed.

narrator-eff4cb2932f2.speaker: narrator
narrator-eff4cb2932f2.text: The grey rind peels away. Inside is a thread of true silver light, still alive. A Silverfruit, nearly sound. You wrap it in a leaf.

narrator-fb7e480288d6.speaker: narrator
narrator-fb7e480288d6.text: The fruit bursts in a puff of grey spores. Everyone coughs and takes three damage.

narrator-acf186040a23.speaker: narrator
narrator-acf186040a23.text: You step back from the trees. They do not thank you, but the leaves stop shivering.

narrator-1f0b1b9ee94c.speaker: narrator
narrator-1f0b1b9ee94c.text: You stand where the cavern roof used to be. The hole is a ragged ring of rock, and through it comes the whole sky.

narrator-fa5cb4c81bac.speaker: narrator
narrator-fa5cb4c81bac.text: It is day, and the sky is a lid of grey cloud. No stars to read. Only the sun, a pale coin, and the long shadow of the gate behind you.

narrator-0b9d02a4ed17.speaker: narrator
narrator-0b9d02a4ed17.text: It is night. Seven stars hang low in the north, over the old gate, like a hand held open.

narrator-ad405d40f442.speaker: narrator
narrator-ad405d40f442.text: The rain falls straight down through the hole and veils half the stars.

narrator-c2b7be84a37c.speaker: narrator
narrator-c2b7be84a37c.text: The mist rises to meet the sky and softens every star into a smudge.

narrator-9dbbbb7a4c87.speaker: narrator
narrator-9dbbbb7a4c87.text: You sit under the broken ring while the light drains out of the cloud. The orchard changes its voice: drip of leaf, tick of rain, a bird that has no business underground. Hours pass. The first star comes out.

narrator-7db152cdcff6.speaker: narrator
narrator-7db152cdcff6.text: The old elves called them the Hand of the Court. Seven stars, and the hand points down, to the keystone of the gate. At midnight the moon will stand exactly there. The gate answers to a song sung in moonlight, with water on its runes.

narrator-4fc9e3b8c145.speaker: narrator
narrator-4fc9e3b8c145.text: The gate's long shadow falls across the grass and ends on a flat stone. Beneath it, a seven pointed star, cut in the rock. The elves marked the hour so no one could forget it: moonlight, a song, and water on the runes.

narrator-cc849662d0b8.speaker: narrator
narrator-cc849662d0b8.text: The cloud shifts, the stars swim, and your neck begins to ache. You lose count somewhere past five. You will have to improvise at the gate.

narrator-f7a2cce4137f.speaker: narrator
narrator-f7a2cce4137f.text: An archway of white stone, carved with leaves and a crescent moon. It is cold, and it is silent. It feels like a door that is waiting for the right person to ask permission. Perhaps the keeper under the bough would know who that is.

narrator-ef0aa235c77f.speaker: narrator
narrator-ef0aa235c77f.text: The gate hums at the edge of hearing, then forgets you. It is waiting for something you do not yet know. Read the trees and the open sky first, then come back.

narrator-01663039cdd4.speaker: narrator
narrator-01663039cdd4.text: The archway is white stone carved with leaves and a crescent moon. A runnel winds through every rune, as if the elves expected the sky to fill it.

narrator-61999466d3d4.speaker: narrator
narrator-61999466d3d4.text: Rain gathers in the runnel and fills the runes with water. They begin to shine.

narrator-4ddd92dbb886.speaker: narrator
narrator-4ddd92dbb886.text: Mist beads in the runnel and the runes weep silver.

narrator-f9a6efe51e39.speaker: narrator
narrator-f9a6efe51e39.text: The crescent moon on the keystone is catching real moonlight from the hole in the roof. It glows.

narrator-e65a2147ec50.speaker: narrator
narrator-e65a2147ec50.text: You know where the moon will stand: directly over the keystone.

narrator-ec2cf10c45cd.speaker: narrator
narrator-ec2cf10c45cd.text: You know the soil below has been salted, and that the gate is choking on it.

narrator-37a02378559e.speaker: narrator
narrator-37a02378559e.text: The heel nail from the grass fits a greasy iron lock hidden under the lowest leaf. The cult built a key.

narrator-c3b5841d6042.speaker: narrator
narrator-c3b5841d6042.text: The runes flare, and the gate throws you back like a wet dog shaking off water. Everyone takes four damage.

narrator-c03e40f40861.speaker: narrator
narrator-c03e40f40861.text: The song comes out of you as if it had been waiting. Water spills down the runnel, light follows the water, and the gate opens like an eyelid. Beyond it a stair of moonlit roots descends into the dark.

narrator-2bab4cd911e5.speaker: narrator
narrator-2bab4cd911e5.text: Far above, the trees shiver. Silver comes back to the leaves, one by one, like lamps being lit.

narrator-c8d449f4b2cd.speaker: narrator
narrator-c8d449f4b2cd.text: You put your shoulder to the keystone and heave. It cracks with a sound like a bone, and the gate swings open crooked, with a gap of silvered dark.

narrator-2470ffb7d6dc.speaker: narrator
narrator-2470ffb7d6dc.text: The trees groan. Somewhere under the earth, something very old opens an eye and is not pleased.

narrator-bbf9f09fd134.speaker: narrator
narrator-bbf9f09fd134.text: The key turns with a greasy click. The gate swings open without a sound, because it has been told to by someone it does not love. Far below, a bell rings once. The cult will know someone has been here.

narrator-ae5c7500913d.speaker: narrator
narrator-ae5c7500913d.text: On the step lies a purse the cult left for whoever opened this door for them. You take it.

narrator-3b2fd4741baf.speaker: narrator
narrator-3b2fd4741baf.text: A knot of roots the width of a door, grown across a stair that leads nowhere yet. Whatever sleeps down there will not wake for you. Not until the gate is open.

narrator-ea6240cb71a9.speaker: narrator
narrator-ea6240cb71a9.text: Beneath the gate, the stair opens into a hollow cut by roots as thick as a man. At its heart a tree no taller than a child glows with silver light. It turns toward you the way a flower turns, and speaks without a mouth.

narrator-3fcc2391aa1f.speaker: narrator
narrator-3fcc2391aa1f.text: The salt will not leave. The roots recoil, and a thorn finds the back of your hand. Everyone takes three damage.

narrator-1440439dffb8.speaker: narrator
narrator-1440439dffb8.text: The hollow gets colder. Everyone takes three damage.

narrator-5c58df76928f.speaker: narrator
narrator-5c58df76928f.text: You kneel, pour out the clean rain from the runnel, and draw the salt out of the roots, a little at a time, until your hands are white to the wrists. The Heartroot sighs.

narrator-eeeb47c8b5e7.speaker: narrator
narrator-eeeb47c8b5e7.text: The Heartroot considers you for the length of three heartbeats, and then a single silver fruit swells at the end of a low branch, and falls into your hand.

narrator-387f66a4fe7c.speaker: narrator
narrator-387f66a4fe7c.text: The blade goes in cleanly. The Heartroot makes no sound, but all the way up the stair you hear the trees begin to groan, one after another, like an audience leaving.

narrator-80bd9d3e3e9c.speaker: narrator
narrator-80bd9d3e3e9c.text: As you reach the oldest tree, silver blossom opens on every branch at once, in the rain or the dark or whatever weather the sky has chosen. Maelis stands among it with her hands over her mouth.

narrator-9fde478bd59c.speaker: narrator
narrator-9fde478bd59c.text: Maelis is waiting under the oldest tree, and she is looking at the staff on your back.

narrator-6a0c9c5ed33f.speaker: narrator
narrator-6a0c9c5ed33f.text: Maelis meets you at the oldest tree. You hold up the Silverfruit, and she takes a long breath.

narrator-82273855edcf.speaker: narrator
narrator-82273855edcf.text: She smiles without looking up. Rain, mist, or stars, the trees are quiet.

narrator-32f1b6b9b880.speaker: narrator
narrator-32f1b6b9b880.text: Grey fruit hangs in hard knots on pale bark. Something is badly wrong with them, but you would not know where to begin. A gardener might. There is a keeper somewhere under the nearest bough.

narrator-3a2e7d23bf74.speaker: narrator
narrator-3a2e7d23bf74.text: The cavern roof has fallen away, and the whole sky stands open above you. It is lovely, and it means nothing to you yet. Ask the keeper of the orchard what she wants read in it.

pip-61ce7fb63231.speaker: pip
pip-61ce7fb63231.text: Garrick Vane. Dead. Three years I waited for that sound, and it is smaller than I thought.

liora-41ea5abf0525.speaker: liora
liora-41ea5abf0525.text: That was not justice. That was a grave dug in anger, and I will not forget it.

brambur-e85caa69682f.speaker: brambur
brambur-e85caa69682f.text: Oh dear. He was begging, wasn't he? I'm not judging. Much. Sorry.

grumsh-206e0fe6cd1e.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-206e0fe6cd1e.text: Some debts are paid only in blood. I do not like it. I understand it.

pip-4feeef8ea0ca.speaker: pip
pip-4feeef8ea0ca.text: You said stop. I heard you. I simply chose not to listen. Old habit.

liora-d6ba752d016e.speaker: liora
liora-d6ba752d016e.text: You told him to stop, and he did not. Remember who leads this road.

fizzwick-1681ae5d85a2.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-1681ae5d85a2.text: Fizzwick observes that the chain of command has been, shall we say, creatively interpreted.

vexrath-ef563cdbb83c.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-ef563cdbb83c.text: An order defied, and a man dead. I shall be writing a very long report.

pip-fef2e241f848.speaker: pip
pip-fef2e241f848.text: I wanted him dead. I still do. But Posy is alive, so... fine. Thank you.

liora-6db55c8d8bb5.speaker: liora
liora-6db55c8d8bb5.text: You chose the harder road. That takes more courage than any blade.

brambur-8f5d4d4277c9.speaker: brambur
brambur-8f5d4d4277c9.text: Oh, bless you. Bless you twice. I was going to cry, and now I can.

zizzy-ba118641ba80.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-ba118641ba80.text: No explosion? Not even a little one? Zizzy is disappointed in a very kind way.

vexrath-b76122718633.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-b76122718633.text: The Watch takes the thief, the town keeps its peace. Order, restored. Splendid.

nettle-973aa06a33e8.speaker: nettle
nettle-973aa06a33e8.text: Handed him straight to the Watch? Dull. I would have struck a better bargain.

pip-30d58d08adbe.speaker: pip
pip-30d58d08adbe.text: Turning a man in. Respectable. Boring, but respectable.

brambur-a10a6474809f.speaker: brambur
brambur-a10a6474809f.text: That seems fair. I think. I hope. Is it fair? It feels fair.

nettle-d8a04bbc4bb0.speaker: nettle
nettle-d8a04bbc4bb0.text: A forger repaying a debt with honest toil. Now that is a good yarn.

brambur-258dd0e0570a.speaker: brambur
brambur-258dd0e0570a.text: Second chances! Mother Pellwen would be so pleased. I am so pleased.

vexrath-bfdb84cdc884.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-bfdb84cdc884.text: A criminal walks on a promise. The law frowns, and so do I.

liora-6248660f2cbe.speaker: liora
liora-6248660f2cbe.text: He will do right by her. I could see it in his face.

pip-2f6d8d002dab.speaker: pip
pip-2f6d8d002dab.text: He ran. Smart man. I would have run too.

vexrath-5ee961c241fc.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-5ee961c241fc.text: A criminal at large, and we watched him go. Disappointing.

nettle-7d05392776d2.speaker: nettle
nettle-7d05392776d2.text: Never corner a man with nothing left to lose. Wisdom, that.

fizzwick-86f06d5b9b11.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-86f06d5b9b11.text: Fizzwick predicted the escape. Fizzwick simply did not mention it.

pip-941441aa1fd9.speaker: pip
pip-941441aa1fd9.text: Hush money. Now that is a language I speak.

zizzy-dc04a5aadd5b.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-dc04a5aadd5b.text: Gold for nothing! Zizzy loves it. Spend it on gunpowder!

liora-c7f774a357af.speaker: liora
liora-c7f774a357af.text: We squeezed a frightened man for coin. I do not like who that makes us.

brambur-000a832d6814.speaker: brambur
brambur-000a832d6814.text: Oh no. Oh, that is a bit mean. Sorry. I am only saying.

brambur-eee2c5b1ddbe.speaker: brambur
brambur-eee2c5b1ddbe.text: They are free. Oh, they are free! I am crying. Sorry. Not sorry.

liora-310d761f6cc7.speaker: liora
liora-310d761f6cc7.text: Let them go home. That is the only right ending to a song like that.

grumsh-b196d9326c95.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-b196d9326c95.text: A good verse. The kind that ends with a door opening.

fizzwick-4a5cfaea2e8a.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-4a5cfaea2e8a.text: Fizzwick contributed morally and acoustically. Mostly morally.

fizzwick-2b3f18e93435.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-2b3f18e93435.text: Binding the Choir. Elegant. Terrifying. Fizzwick approves, privately.

brambur-d247431209ca.speaker: brambur
brambur-d247431209ca.text: Oh, but they were people. They were someone's sisters. I am so sorry.

liora-24ce0d988aa3.speaker: liora
liora-24ce0d988aa3.text: You chained a sorrow to your belt. I hope it does not sing to you at night.

nettle-1bfe23bc2ec1.speaker: nettle
nettle-1bfe23bc2ec1.text: A bound choir. Now that is a tale worth drinking to, and a debt worth avoiding.

zizzy-47b34fd506c6.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-47b34fd506c6.text: Smash! Zizzy loves it when a plan is also a hammer.

fizzwick-9c4dab2780a2.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-9c4dab2780a2.text: A masterwork of the optical arts, destroyed. Fizzwick will weep. Briefly.

grumsh-96376bcfd242.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-96376bcfd242.text: Some things should not see us. Good riddance.

pip-5f780b874ec8.speaker: pip
pip-5f780b874ec8.text: Seven years bad luck. Fine. I was already on a streak.

fizzwick-2f4ea1aa586c.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-2f4ea1aa586c.text: Fizzwick gazed into the Sovereign's own glass and lived! Do write that down.

liora-7e26917f5b3a.speaker: liora
liora-7e26917f5b3a.text: You looked, knowing he would see you. That was brave. And foolish.

brambur-9b9707c8fd58.speaker: brambur
brambur-9b9707c8fd58.text: It saw us! It saw all of us! I will light a candle. Several candles.

pip-ce4be1fa0096.speaker: pip
pip-ce4be1fa0096.text: Knowledge is a weapon. I like a weapon. I just wish it did not look back.

vexrath-68a671277c0e.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-68a671277c0e.text: The truth, however bitter, is the only honourable coin. Well spoken.

liora-3c1ae380c48b.speaker: liora
liora-3c1ae380c48b.text: He deserved to know. So did his men. Thank you for telling him.

grumsh-dafed5551d20.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-dafed5551d20.text: The dead are owed the truth. Few remember that.

pip-853a57d7ff08.speaker: pip
pip-853a57d7ff08.text: Honest with a ghost. Bold. I would have lied and slept fine.

pip-10c1b2f9416c.speaker: pip
pip-10c1b2f9416c.text: A kind lie. Best sort there is. He rests, and nobody gets hurt.

nettle-9845a1326e6e.speaker: nettle
nettle-9845a1326e6e.text: Ah, a fine fib told for a good cause. I could not have done it better.

vexrath-f9aa7076b930.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-f9aa7076b930.text: You lied to a Warden of the Crown. I will pretend I was elsewhere.

liora-cc605d48de05.speaker: liora
liora-cc605d48de05.text: A kind lie. I do not love it. But I saw his face, so I will not argue.

liora-77014245dcc8.speaker: liora
liora-77014245dcc8.text: Listen. The trees are singing again. You woke them gently, and they know it.

fizzwick-d21d542e1aa7.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-d21d542e1aa7.text: The old rite, correctly performed. Fizzwick is pleased. Mostly with himself.

brambur-caa4a463081c.speaker: brambur
brambur-caa4a463081c.text: It worked! The roots are glowing! Sorry, trees. Well done, trees.

grumsh-ff5252a590bf.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-ff5252a590bf.text: A quiet door, opened quietly. I like that.

zizzy-fcf280e6bbc0.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-fcf280e6bbc0.text: We kicked the door! Zizzy approves! Subtlety is for people who cannot blow things up!

grumsh-b24397e1675b.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-b24397e1675b.text: Open, but crooked. Like most things I have forced.

liora-f928d93a6654.speaker: liora
liora-f928d93a6654.text: You broke an elven gate. It will remember that, and so will I.

brambur-0e06179633c7.speaker: brambur
brambur-0e06179633c7.text: Oh, the poor gate. It was so old. Sorry, sorry, sorry.

nettle-d0cc2fafb596.speaker: nettle
nettle-d0cc2fafb596.text: Using the cult's own key! Poetic. I would have charged admission.

pip-66fd53e6c71c.speaker: pip
pip-66fd53e6c71c.text: Stolen key, stolen door. I am beginning to like you.

vexrath-d342ca358541.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-d342ca358541.text: We opened sacred ground with a cultist's key. I have concerns.

liora-3a2451ab1f17.speaker: liora
liora-3a2451ab1f17.text: The gate opened, and a seal broke. That was not worth it.

liora-cb2452db0e2f.speaker: liora
liora-cb2452db0e2f.text: You healed the Heartroot without asking for anything. That is rare.

brambur-5dc95be9a97b.speaker: brambur
brambur-5dc95be9a97b.text: The roots are drinking! Oh, that is lovely. Well done, truly.

grumsh-f1fb08482f1c.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-f1fb08482f1c.text: A garden saved. Not every poem ends so well.

zizzy-84a2efa35875.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-84a2efa35875.text: You cleaned a tree. Zizzy would have burned the weeds. Zizzy respects your way, though.

liora-9c8998c0d62f.speaker: liora
liora-9c8998c0d62f.text: The Heartroot trusts you. I have not seen that in years.

nettle-fbc2e58e58cd.speaker: nettle
nettle-fbc2e58e58cd.text: You asked it nicely and it gave you fruit. Best negotiation I have ever seen.

brambur-1bbf0f2f703b.speaker: brambur
brambur-1bbf0f2f703b.text: It gave us a gift! Mother Pellwen is showing off.

fizzwick-f38d007afb63.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-f38d007afb63.text: Fizzwick notes that politeness is, apparently, a spell.

pip-04c49ecffd8f.speaker: pip
pip-04c49ecffd8f.text: One graft, one fortune. Do not look at me like that. It is a good trade.

nettle-9812182c629d.speaker: nettle
nettle-9812182c629d.text: Cut a branch from a sacred tree and sold the splinters. Is it wrong that I admire it?

liora-9a9a1865bd35.speaker: liora
liora-9a9a1865bd35.text: The trees groaned when you cut it. I heard them. You did too.

brambur-5ab5a2336eed.speaker: brambur
brambur-5ab5a2336eed.text: Oh no. Oh, the poor tree. Sorry. I am so sorry.

liora-cb9781eda483.speaker: liora
liora-cb9781eda483.text: Home. Yes. That is the only word that matters, and you said it first.

brambur-200b2fcd2648.speaker: brambur
brambur-200b2fcd2648.text: I will help. I will carry the bandages. Let us bring her home.

pip-3b55eb3bbd8a.speaker: pip
pip-3b55eb3bbd8a.text: Bring her home. Lovely. Someone should bring Posy home as well.

vexrath-9623506462a7.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-9623506462a7.text: A vow properly sworn is binding. I shall hold you to it.

grumsh-d66c6e524a05.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-d66c6e524a05.text: Malthrax will kneel. The tower will know it. I will write the verse.

zizzy-56705392ad6b.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-56705392ad6b.text: Kneel! He will kneel! Zizzy will bring the powder!

brambur-71062bf74332.speaker: brambur
brambur-71062bf74332.text: Kneeling is a strong word. Could we maybe... ask him to sit?

liora-b7990687eeb5.speaker: liora
liora-b7990687eeb5.text: Bold words. Let us make sure you can pay for them.

zizzy-1b45c70f4bd1.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-1b45c70f4bd1.text: Controlled demolition! Zizzy is so proud of you.

brambur-6b1c4c540b23.speaker: brambur
brambur-6b1c4c540b23.text: The cultists! Under the... oh. Sorry, cultists.

pip-bb4bf092b570.speaker: pip
pip-bb4bf092b570.text: Why fight them when the ceiling will do it for free?

vexrath-844759e97e88.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-844759e97e88.text: A tidy solution. Structurally unsound, morally grey. Efficient.

brambur-e37670151f69.speaker: brambur
brambur-e37670151f69.text: You know, I think I stopped being afraid of you somewhere around the last door. Thank you.

fizzwick-69d3deab949a.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-69d3deab949a.text: Fizzwick has decided you are almost as clever as Fizzwick. This is the highest honour he bestows.

pip-177265919678.speaker: pip
pip-177265919678.text: I do not trust people. I trust you a little. Do not make me regret it.

grumsh-55b9dc62a7af.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-55b9dc62a7af.text: I will put your name in a verse. A good one. The kind that survives the tower.

zizzy-9c4f919c93ef.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-9c4f919c93ef.text: You are my favourite party member! The explosions are only second favourite!

vexrath-f8789e8ab516.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-f8789e8ab516.text: My clan would have called you worthy. I have decided to agree with them.

nettle-44c603e6720d.speaker: nettle
nettle-44c603e6720d.text: In all my tall tales, the hero had a face like yours. Remarkable coincidence, that.

liora-2b37da5489fd.speaker: liora
liora-2b37da5489fd.text: My father would have liked you. I think that is the best thing I can say.

brambur-48aa3f194158.speaker: brambur
brambur-48aa3f194158.text: I do not like how quiet I have become around you. Sorry. I just wanted you to know.

fizzwick-0ef74edda444.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-0ef74edda444.text: Fizzwick is composing a strongly worded footnote about your recent decisions.

pip-72521fa22657.speaker: pip
pip-72521fa22657.text: You keep making choices I cannot forgive. I am still here. Do not push it.

grumsh-3d2488361b75.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-3d2488361b75.text: The verse I am writing about you is a short one, and it ends badly.

zizzy-ff05354f1182.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-ff05354f1182.text: This is not as fun as it used to be. Just saying.

vexrath-27c6016522e6.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-27c6016522e6.text: I follow you because I swore to. Do not mistake that for approval.

nettle-39470a6108ea.speaker: nettle
nettle-39470a6108ea.text: I have sailed with villains who made me feel better about myself than you do.

liora-c9d80b15c6b5.speaker: liora
liora-c9d80b15c6b5.text: I will keep walking beside you. But I will be watching what you do.

narrator-497674faf539.speaker: narrator
narrator-497674faf539.text: Pip's jaw tightens. She believes it, and perhaps you should too.

dmj-80c9a7e9f9ca.speaker: dm
dmj-80c9a7e9f9ca.text: The roof of the world has fallen away, and open sky pours down on the Sunken Orchard. Rain whispers through old silver trees, and an elven gate waits among them, patient as a held breath.

dmj-40027d3ebca5.speaker: dm
dmj-40027d3ebca5.text: The old kiln is a cavern of warm brick, and in its heart stands the Mirror, tall as a door and framed in black iron. It shows you the room as it will be in an hour, and it does not blink.

dmj-27511ef9b220.speaker: dm
dmj-27511ef9b220.text: The tunnel widens into a nest of gnawed bones and stolen cutlery, heaped into a lopsided throne. Something large and orcish stirs on top of it, and beside it the Broodmother clicks her fangs. Roll for initiative.

dmj-6b4d55d95c1d.speaker: dm
dmj-6b4d55d95c1d.text: The cave drops into a drowned amphitheatre, black and mirror still. Then the water parts, and Old Clubtail rises with his wasps humming round him like a crown. Steady now, heroes.

dmj-5eccd7490063.speaker: dm
dmj-5eccd7490063.text: Crystals grow in a perfect ring around a pedestal of black glass. Gargoyles lean from the shadows, and in the centre Glasshide the Basilisk lifts her eyes. Do not look her in the face.

dmj-c9de2f2e1f15.speaker: dm
dmj-c9de2f2e1f15.text: The forge hall opens around an anvil the size of a wagon, glowing white hot. Forgemaster Brakk steps out of the smoke with Cindermaw at his heel, and the hammer in his fist is far too fine for him.

dmj-e8d2ff760a51.speaker: dm
dmj-e8d2ff760a51.text: At the heart of the vault, a crown of black iron rises from the dark, and beneath it sits Malthrax, the Dread Sovereign himself. He smiles like a man who has been expecting you. Every die at this table is about to matter.

dmj-29ecfa755709.speaker: dm
dmj-29ecfa755709.text: The floor splits like rotten wood, and the Tyrant of the Blackspire climbs up out of the dark. Gorvax is awake, and he is hungry. Steel yourselves, for this is the last roll.

dmj-757544ea3a6b.speaker: dm
dmj-757544ea3a6b.text: In the dust lies an iron key, cold and heavy with purpose. The way down is yours to open.

dmj-e670f6097bb9.speaker: dm
dmj-e670f6097bb9.text: From the silt of the grotto you lift a key, green with weed and still as sharp as the day it was cut.

dmj-127ba40252cf.speaker: dm
dmj-127ba40252cf.text: A key of pale crystal rests in your palm, and it hums, very softly, in the same sad tune as the cavern.

dmj-7bb2a4687152.speaker: dm
dmj-7bb2a4687152.text: The Ashforge key is still warm from the fire that made it. Someone left in a hurry.

dmj-fde561337e64.speaker: dm
dmj-fde561337e64.text: The final key is black and heavy as a verdict. Beyond it, one door remains.

dmj-cf7cd6ebd9e5.speaker: dm
dmj-cf7cd6ebd9e5.text: Light spills from the treasure like a promise kept. Not every adventurer lives long enough to hold something so fine.

dmj-b9e0a5116e6a.speaker: dm
dmj-b9e0a5116e6a.text: The named brute lies still. Somewhere in the Spire, someone is going to hear about this.

dmj-43ada74f67aa.speaker: dm
dmj-43ada74f67aa.text: A halfling's grudge is a quiet thing, until it is not. Lantern Row left its mark on these halls, and the road to Garrick Vane runs through every floor.

dmj-6d1afb470a1b.speaker: dm
dmj-6d1afb470a1b.text: In Emberhollow, a pawnbroker is being robbed in her own name. Somebody forged her hand, and somebody else is digging up the dead.

dmj-f21e7f2a06c7.speaker: dm
dmj-f21e7f2a06c7.text: A fisherman's wife went down to the grotto shrine to sing, and the water kept her songs. Harl Tollow waits on the shore, and he has almost stopped hoping.

dmj-51f8c0d79fc1.speaker: dm
dmj-51f8c0d79fc1.text: A glasswright asks you to destroy her finest work. It stands in the old kiln, and it has been watching since the day it was made.

dmj-953dd0c0af5a.speaker: dm
dmj-953dd0c0af5a.text: A sergeant dead three years still keeps his post, and he cannot rest until he knows what became of his three missing soldiers.

dmj-89c82abd1e99.speaker: dm
dmj-89c82abd1e99.text: Maelis Dewbough tends the Orchard like a garden of old graves. Something is rotting its heartwood, and the grey fruit is telling her so.

dmj-76ae95b4e0ff.speaker: dm
dmj-76ae95b4e0ff.text: The Seneschal of Keys turns from his ledger, unhurried, and he is smiling. Behind him a small voice cries out, and everyone at this table knows whose it is.

dmj-c6a8bb7d468b.speaker: dm
dmj-c6a8bb7d468b.text: Roots as old as the Spire coil round a pool of black water, and in it a pale light turns, slowly, like an eye. The Heartroot is listening. Choose your words with care.

dmj-f099fa498dba.speaker: dm
dmj-f099fa498dba.text: The hammer falls, and the Mirror sighs rather than shatters. Ten eyes go dark one by one, and far below, something loses its sight.

dmj-9db3f7fcdb3c.speaker: dm
dmj-9db3f7fcdb3c.text: You look, and the Mirror shows you everything it has ever seen. Now you know where the staff will break, and the Sovereign knows your face. A seal cracks in the dark.

dmj-4a12b669a911.speaker: dm
dmj-4a12b669a911.text: The release verse rings out, and the Sisters of the Tide rise from the black water, singing. They go home at last.

dmj-97a07df479b4.speaker: dm
dmj-97a07df479b4.text: The Choir's song bends to your will, and the Sisters fall silent, bound. The water shivers as though it were weeping.

dmj-ba9b49e742f4.speaker: dm
dmj-ba9b49e742f4.text: The old rite sounds, and the Gate of the Silver Court wakes. One by one the trees light up, and a stair of roots leads down.

dmj-5c9923a5e309.speaker: dm
dmj-5c9923a5e309.text: The seal breaks with a crack like a bone, and the gate stands open, but crooked. Something beneath it is very angry.

dmj-3607c308ff75.speaker: dm
dmj-3607c308ff75.text: The brine key turns, and the gate opens as if it had always belonged to the cult. Far below, a bell rings, and a seal cracks.

dmj-bcb921054ba5.speaker: dm
dmj-bcb921054ba5.text: Garrick Vane falls, and a debt of three long years is paid in a single breath. Pip does not speak, and the table is very quiet.

dmj-406c5cbc1e66.speaker: dm
dmj-406c5cbc1e66.text: You lower the blade, and a sparrow of hope flies out of a three year cage. Somewhere on Cant Street, a girl named Posy is waiting to be found.

dmj-bf05cb39f6c2.speaker: dm
dmj-bf05cb39f6c2.text: The law takes its due, and Odalys Fenn's name is clean again. Justice has been served, cold and tidy.

dmj-301f06ed6f79.speaker: dm
dmj-301f06ed6f79.text: A forger repays his debt with honest work, and the town never learns the tale. Sometimes mercy is the better coin.

dmj-994ce82d1da7.speaker: dm
dmj-994ce82d1da7.text: The forger bolts into the night, and the pawnbroker's name is cleared, though her purse is lighter. Not every story ends with a bow.

dmj-5476b4bea462.speaker: dm
dmj-5476b4bea462.text: The silver is heavy in your hand, and the silence you bought is heavier still. Some coins leave a stain.

dmj-d6e800322886.speaker: dm
dmj-d6e800322886.text: Harl Tollow weeps on the shore, and for the first time in years, it is a good weeping. The Sisters are free.

dmj-43fa855537ad.speaker: dm
dmj-43fa855537ad.text: Harl Tollow learns what became of the Choir, and he does not thank you. A bargain has been struck, and its price is not yet paid.

dmj-0ea92ba7b919.speaker: dm
dmj-0ea92ba7b919.text: Ysolde Verrin is free of her Mirror, and a thousand shards of silver lie across the kiln floor. She presses a circlet into your hand and does not look back.

dmj-abfb1cfae35a.speaker: dm
dmj-abfb1cfae35a.text: Ysolde listens to what you saw, and she does not lecture. A glasswright knows exactly what a mirror costs.

dmj-69f8d781143d.speaker: dm
dmj-69f8d781143d.text: The truth is a hard coin, but Sergeant Crane takes it gladly. His ghost will stand beside you at the end.

dmj-c85a3d8e673a.speaker: dm
dmj-c85a3d8e673a.text: A kind lie is told, and a restless soldier is finally at peace. The Wardens' last roll is settled.

dmj-91588ca91774.speaker: dm
dmj-91588ca91774.text: Spring comes early to the Sunken Orchard. Silver blossom drifts through the rain, and Maelis Dewbough laughs aloud.

dmj-80d6a9a0824f.speaker: dm
dmj-80d6a9a0824f.text: The Heartroot trusts you with its fruit, and Maelis trusts you with her mother's wreath. A rare thing, in any age.

dmj-1dbf2c9f3d34.speaker: dm
dmj-1dbf2c9f3d34.text: The trees groan as you leave. Maelis takes your coin, but she will not meet your eye, and you will not be welcome here in spring.

dmj-3b78239ec1e6.speaker: dm
dmj-3b78239ec1e6.text: Down you go, brave souls, into the Rat Warrens, where the straw is damp and the cheese is older than the town. A thousand tiny eyes blink out as your torchlight finds them, and somewhere a bell no bigger than a soup tin begins to ring.

dmj-7d3a8b8eaf25.speaker: dm
dmj-7d3a8b8eaf25.text: Cold water swallows your boots, and the Drowned Grotto yawns wide around you. Pale lights drift under the black pools, and something very large turns over in its sleep.

dmj-daccd98a8a85.speaker: dm
dmj-daccd98a8a85.text: The Glimmerdeep opens like the inside of a jewel, and every crystal hums the same sorrowful note. A hundred reflections march beside you, and not one of them keeps step.

dmj-bf1646cb0752.speaker: dm
dmj-bf1646cb0752.text: Heat strikes your face like an opened oven door. Slag crawls through the old dwarf channels, and the hammers of the Ashforge ring on, though no smith is left to swing them.

dmj-df929242fcce.speaker: dm
dmj-df929242fcce.text: Silence falls over you like a coffin lid. Pillars carved with roaring lizards climb into the dark, and the air trembles with the slow breathing of something that has waited a very long age.

dmj-3ed82cf32abb.speaker: dm
dmj-3ed82cf32abb.text: Back in the Rat-Warrens. The scratching starts up again.

dmj-f5c72615823b.speaker: dm
dmj-f5c72615823b.text: The Drowned Grotto. Cold water closes over your boots once more.

dmj-27beacd47762.speaker: dm
dmj-27beacd47762.text: The Glimmerdeep hums its single note. Your reflections are waiting.

dmj-92bfd56cf939.speaker: dm
dmj-92bfd56cf939.text: The Ashforge heat greets you like an old, bad-tempered friend.

dmj-be06dc8a2a14.speaker: dm
dmj-be06dc8a2a14.text: The Vault. The breathing has not stopped.

dmj-00a876dd1952.speaker: dm
dmj-00a876dd1952.text: Here the rat-sign stops, as if even the vermin give this spot a wide berth. Something waits here that is not a rat.

dmj-fdeddfde6919.speaker: dm
dmj-fdeddfde6919.text: Clear water bubbles from a cracked basin carved with a smiling face. It smells, astonishingly, of mint.

dmj-b4d1c4c33c02.speaker: dm
dmj-b4d1c4c33c02.text: A spiral stair corkscrews down into the dark. A cold draught rises from it, carrying the smell of standing water.

dmj-e7b40c694e6a.speaker: dm
dmj-e7b40c694e6a.text: The hidden passage is lined with tiny claw-marked tallies. Someone, or several someones, has been counting days here.

dmj-327b80946f51.speaker: dm
dmj-327b80946f51.text: A low chamber stacked with mouldy grain sacks, every one of them gnawed open. The floor crunches underfoot, and you decide not to look down.

dmj-f45e1ef5e9d7.speaker: dm
dmj-f45e1ef5e9d7.text: Dozens of tiny shrines line this room: thimbles, buttons and bent nails arranged with real devotion around a portrait of a very fat rat.

dmj-8d398a0537ca.speaker: dm
dmj-8d398a0537ca.text: Water pools in the middle of this chamber, and the walls are furred with nests of shredded cloth. The smell is magnificent, in the worst way.

dmj-d9f30bfe51c0.speaker: dm
dmj-d9f30bfe51c0.text: Old smuggler's crates rot in the corners, stamped with the crest of Emberhollow. One still rattles faintly when you pass.

dmj-9d6badccf754.speaker: dm
dmj-9d6badccf754.text: A ring of half-sunken lanterns marks this place, each one still somehow burning beneath the water.

dmj-ed9ae9d40880.speaker: dm
dmj-ed9ae9d40880.text: A spring of warm, glowing water rises here, fizzing gently. The fungus around it grows in the shape of open hands.

dmj-e09c7b2b93d5.speaker: dm
dmj-e09c7b2b93d5.text: Steps slick with algae lead down past a waterline carved with the warning "HIGH TIDE". The ink is fresh.

dmj-8a9ebb9efd23.speaker: dm
dmj-8a9ebb9efd23.text: Behind the false wall is a dry pocket of air that smells of old parchment. Someone hid here while the water rose.

dmj-0569952d3f06.speaker: dm
dmj-0569952d3f06.text: A flooded hall where bioluminescent eels drift between broken columns, lighting the water in slow blue pulses.

dmj-8e51f5cf02f0.speaker: dm
dmj-8e51f5cf02f0.text: Shipwreck timbers jut from the walls of this cave, though the sea is miles away. A barnacled figurehead watches you pass.

dmj-c7450fdaf8aa.speaker: dm
dmj-c7450fdaf8aa.text: Stalactites drip in this grotto like a broken water clock. The pools below are full of tiny white crabs that click in unison.

dmj-9a1ea6db9271.speaker: dm
dmj-9a1ea6db9271.text: Nets heavy with old catches hang from the ceiling here. Some of the catches are wearing boots.

dmj-75f9ddc8e0b8.speaker: dm
dmj-75f9ddc8e0b8.text: The hum of the crystals drops to a low, almost-words murmur here, as if the cavern is trying to tell you something.

dmj-ae00794a10da.speaker: dm
dmj-ae00794a10da.text: A pool of liquid starlight shimmers in a crystal bowl. Drinking it tastes like the first cold breath of winter.

dmj-7de588c09d6b.speaker: dm
dmj-7de588c09d6b.text: A crystal stair spirals downward, each step chiming a note as you test it. The tune is not a happy one.

dmj-22e454f641f3.speaker: dm
dmj-22e454f641f3.text: The concealed grotto is dark: no crystals, no reflections, no hum. The silence is the loudest thing you have heard all day.

dmj-bc62f88d53d3.speaker: dm
dmj-bc62f88d53d3.text: A gallery of statues frozen mid-stride, each one carrying a mirror that was raised a moment too late.

dmj-369fdb67673f.speaker: dm
dmj-369fdb67673f.text: Huge amethyst columns split the light into slow purple rainbows. The floor is warm, and faintly ticks like cooling glass.

dmj-ac3d17dd266b.speaker: dm
dmj-ac3d17dd266b.text: A garden of luminous mushrooms grows in a perfect spiral here. Stepping off the path makes them all turn to face you.

dmj-e000cba1c7c8.speaker: dm
dmj-e000cba1c7c8.text: Shards of a shattered geode the size of a cottage litter this chamber, still humming with whatever broke out of it.

dmj-0e20c41ef8de.speaker: dm
dmj-0e20c41ef8de.text: Here the hammer-song stops. Tools lie where they were dropped, mid-swing, and the air smells of a hasty departure.

dmj-449c0988ab03.speaker: dm
dmj-449c0988ab03.text: Cool water pours from the mouth of a stone dwarf into a quenching trough. Steam curls up, smelling of iron and relief.

dmj-53ab77840203.speaker: dm
dmj-53ab77840203.text: A brass-railed stair plunges into dark heat. Each step down is a little warmer, and the walls start to sweat.

dmj-02eb08231bba.speaker: dm
dmj-02eb08231bba.text: A hidden smithy, its tools neatly hung and its coals banked as if the smith stepped out for lunch a hundred years ago.

dmj-e63192e04923.speaker: dm
dmj-e63192e04923.text: A chamber of cooling moulds, each one shaped like a different weapon. Several of the moulds are empty and still warm.

dmj-f32bc1223e42.speaker: dm
dmj-f32bc1223e42.text: Bellows the size of houses wheeze in this hall, pushed by nothing you can see. Embers dance in the draught.

dmj-9dc1240b2637.speaker: dm
dmj-9dc1240b2637.text: An ore-cart track loops through this cavern, and a cart full of glowing slag still creaks slowly along it.

dmj-93c7575fa67e.speaker: dm
dmj-93c7575fa67e.text: Racks of half-finished armour line the walls here, helmets turned so that every empty visor watches the door.

dmj-4f41071a3f73.speaker: dm
dmj-4f41071a3f73.text: Old murals here show tiny heroes fleeing a towering lizard. The last panel has been scratched out with claws.

dmj-9bc1cef621ce.speaker: dm
dmj-9bc1cef621ce.text: A basin of violet light pulses slowly, like a resting heartbeat. The pain of the road drains away as you drink.

dmj-87cdec04142e.speaker: dm
dmj-87cdec04142e.text: Elowen's light pours from the altar ahead, golden and steady. Five keyholes wait around its rim.

dmj-c9384da7cdcf.speaker: dm
dmj-c9384da7cdcf.text: This hidden alcove holds the bones of a knight in mirrored armour, one hand still pointing toward the vault.

dmj-a77256f6cb40.speaker: dm
dmj-a77256f6cb40.text: Eggshells as big as barrels lie cracked open across this chamber. Whatever hatched has had a long time to grow.

dmj-73bd2dd724d8.speaker: dm
dmj-73bd2dd724d8.text: Carved pillars of roaring lizards hold up a ceiling lost in darkness. Rain-sound echoes from far above, though there is no sky.

dmj-639a646642ca.speaker: dm
dmj-639a646642ca.text: A trophy hall of crushed shields and bent swords, each tagged with a name in neat, patient handwriting.

dmj-8bba228827e7.speaker: dm
dmj-8bba228827e7.text: The floor here is scorched in a long, perfect line, as if lightning once ran along it on four legs.

dmj-7b4c6e5d13e0.speaker: dm
dmj-7b4c6e5d13e0.text: Emberhollow huddles beneath the black shadow of the Spire, all slate roofs and leaning chimneys. The bell tolls the hour a little nervously, and every face in the square has lost someone to the dark below.

dmj-8f8a670b8d08.speaker: dm
dmj-8f8a670b8d08.text: The Boar & Spoon is warm, loud and smells of spilled ale, roast onions and wet dog. A fiddler saws at something cheerful in the corner while a mounted boar's head, wearing a spoon on a string, watches the door. Adventurers swap tall tales at long tables, and every one of them has a story about the Blackspire.

dmj-28f49355f55e.speaker: dm
dmj-28f49355f55e.text: The Temple of Cant is cool and hushed, lit by tall candles that never quite drip. Incense of cedar and myrrh drifts past a donation box the size of a coffin. Somewhere a priest is counting coins very quietly.

dmj-8bd3cbc0ad78.speaker: dm
dmj-8bd3cbc0ad78.text: Straw dummies hang from posts in the Training Grounds, most of them missing their heads. The air rings with clashing steel, barked orders and the thud of arrows striking targets. A grizzled sergeant watches you sideways and mutters something about soft hands.

dmj-ae9bdf17af22.speaker: dm
dmj-ae9bdf17af22.text: Fizzbang's Trading Post is an avalanche of goods waiting to happen: ropes, lanterns, potions and at least one suspicious barrel. It smells of lamp oil and lavender soap. A gnome peers at you over a counter piled high with "bargains".

dmj-a0714f6b37db.speaker: dm
dmj-a0714f6b37db.text: The cobbles end at a ring of standing stones around a gaping stair. Cold air breathes up from below, carrying faint echoes: a drip, a scratch, something like distant laughter. The town's last lantern swings above the entrance, and nobody has ever bothered to light it.

tilda-6a7532d6cabb.speaker: tilda
tilda-6a7532d6cabb.text: They say a halfling put Garrick Vane in the ground. Lantern Row held a vigil.

brogan-09d5810eaec6.speaker: brogan
brogan-09d5810eaec6.text: Hard justice. I will not say I blame her.

tilda-7b1f6306cff9.speaker: tilda
tilda-7b1f6306cff9.text: I heard the halfling let Garrick Vane walk. Mercy, in Lantern Row!

ketter-6c1aaa47123c.speaker: ketter
ketter-6c1aaa47123c.text: It takes more nerve to spare a man than to stab him.

iolen-5b090abee38c.speaker: iolen
iolen-5b090abee38c.text: The Sisters sing free now. Harl Tollow rows out, and the water answers him.

iolen-73388761f408.speaker: iolen
iolen-73388761f408.text: The Drowned Choir sings for a master now. Harl has stopped rowing.

mosk-070212e31a56.speaker: mosk
mosk-070212e31a56.text: A song with a leash on it. I do not like it.

mosk-816d5213930a.speaker: mosk
mosk-816d5213930a.text: Ysolde's Mirror is shards on the kiln floor. The glasswright sleeps at last.

tilda-569a94f1ef45.speaker: tilda
tilda-569a94f1ef45.text: Silver glitter in every boot that comes up from the Glimmerdeep.

iolen-9416786fd241.speaker: iolen
iolen-9416786fd241.text: Someone looked into the Mirror, I am told. They came out knowing things.

ketter-2dbb6a105519.speaker: ketter
ketter-2dbb6a105519.text: I once saw a man go quiet after a mirror. He was never the same.

brogan-122e2bbfa12d.speaker: brogan
brogan-122e2bbfa12d.text: Odalys named the forger to their face. Pawn tickets are honest again.

tilda-3bd4a21bc0d8.speaker: tilda
tilda-3bd4a21bc0d8.text: Whoever pointed the finger had proof. Nobody is arguing.

tilda-26edec56785e.speaker: tilda
tilda-26edec56785e.text: The forger left town by lantern light, and Odalys looks lighter.

mosk-a675de9f4648.speaker: mosk
mosk-a675de9f4648.text: I heard coins changed hands. I heard nothing else. I heard nothing.

iolen-2203fa629dfd.speaker: iolen
iolen-2203fa629dfd.text: The Sunken Orchard blooms again under open sky. Silverfruit in the market!

brogan-f76e8abe2e36.speaker: brogan
brogan-f76e8abe2e36.text: One bite and my cough was gone.

iolen-538a77b7ad7f.speaker: iolen
iolen-538a77b7ad7f.text: The orchard gate stands crooked and the trees have gone quiet.

mosk-eeb0d8de3889.speaker: mosk
mosk-eeb0d8de3889.text: Somebody paid a price down there. I bar my door at night.

ketter-eb39cf50576e.speaker: ketter
ketter-eb39cf50576e.text: The Sergeant of the Fourth Company has his roll called at last. You gave him peace.

brogan-252e4d194c48.speaker: brogan
brogan-252e4d194c48.text: Skarn the Spider Rider is dead! The Warrens are quiet. Mostly.

tilda-691811f2c6a0.speaker: tilda
tilda-691811f2c6a0.text: The rats never read the news, love.

tilda-a8fe45c44850.speaker: tilda
tilda-a8fe45c44850.text: Old Clubtail is down! Miners say the Grotto doors open easier now.

mosk-60554f3ccfc7.speaker: mosk
mosk-60554f3ccfc7.text: Glasshide fell. The Glimmerdeep glows, and nobody has turned to glass this week.

ketter-a95bfb71be0f.speaker: ketter
ketter-a95bfb71be0f.text: Forgemaster Brakk is finished. The Ashforge anvils ring for free folk again.

tilda-62d60f50011a.speaker: tilda
tilda-62d60f50011a.text: The Dread Sovereign is dead! Somebody drinks free tonight. I hope it is you.

ketter-790a14a3d1b7.speaker: ketter
ketter-790a14a3d1b7.text: The Tyrant still sleeps under the vault, mind. Do not celebrate too long.

iolen-2dc127a356af.speaker: iolen
iolen-2dc127a356af.text: The moon looks cracked tonight. One seal is gone, they say.

brogan-a85cb29581c8.speaker: brogan
brogan-a85cb29581c8.text: Every third rest, another one breaks. Count your naps.

ketter-726bd379a772.speaker: ketter
ketter-726bd379a772.text: Three seals broken. Gorvax shifts in his sleep. Do not linger up here.

tilda-3b5634432a3c.speaker: tilda
tilda-3b5634432a3c.text: Odalys at the pawn shop is white as flour. Someone forged her tickets.

mosk-bad8d548c539.speaker: mosk
mosk-bad8d548c539.text: If you find the forger, she pays well. If you do not, she remembers.

ketter-80554f2becba.speaker: ketter
ketter-80554f2becba.text: Three leads at the pawn shop: the tickets, the grave dirt, the back alley. Check all three first.

tilda-c61e8a26bad8.speaker: tilda
tilda-c61e8a26bad8.text: Odalys wants proof, not a guess. A hasty accusation never ends well.

iolen-08f62d3c8634.speaker: iolen
iolen-08f62d3c8634.text: Harl Tollow rows out each dusk and listens. He swears his wife still sings under the water.

brogan-51323bb59090.speaker: brogan
brogan-51323bb59090.text: Down in the Drowned Grotto, second floor. You need a strong stomach.

iolen-782d569a7697.speaker: iolen
iolen-782d569a7697.text: The Sunken Chapel stands on the second floor. The Black Pool lies beyond it. Bring a steady heart.

ketter-64b4109152da.speaker: ketter
ketter-64b4109152da.text: A glasswright named Ysolde lost her trust in mirrors. The old kiln, third floor.

mosk-5d70f9d610ad.speaker: mosk
mosk-5d70f9d610ad.text: Do not look at any mirror down there longer than you must.

ketter-941ce08c91dd.speaker: ketter
ketter-941ce08c91dd.text: A Sergeant of the Fourth Company still walks the Ashforge, counting his dead.

brogan-4fcd2d96e73c.speaker: brogan
brogan-4fcd2d96e73c.text: Three tags missing from his roll. Search the old barracks.

iolen-436571e8fcf7.speaker: iolen
iolen-436571e8fcf7.text: A keeper named Maelis tends the Sunken Orchard on the third floor. The trees listen.

iolen-97a2dd098143.speaker: iolen
iolen-97a2dd098143.text: They answer to the hour and the weather. Read the sky and the trees before you choose.

tilda-fcb93d129a2e.speaker: tilda
tilda-fcb93d129a2e.text: Chalk marks on the cellar doors in Lantern Row. Three dots and a hook. Still fresh.

brogan-32ce625be4ad.speaker: brogan
brogan-32ce625be4ad.text: Garrick Vane's old crew. Eleven gone, and one man walks free.

brogan-46c0592502d9.speaker: brogan
brogan-46c0592502d9.text: Four of the Watch went into the Warrens and never came back. Rowan will not say it.

ketter-a2c9bd58640a.speaker: ketter
ketter-a2c9bd58640a.text: Bound, not dead, I would bet my knee. Cut them loose.

tilda-3aabdcee13c7.speaker: tilda
tilda-3aabdcee13c7.text: Marga hears digging under the cellar. Not rats. Someone tunnels toward the barrels.

mosk-7d44bfe15edc.speaker: mosk
mosk-7d44bfe15edc.text: First floor, I heard. Collapse it and she will never stop thanking you.

iolen-d4369fac12c1.speaker: iolen
iolen-d4369fac12c1.text: Brother Osric lost temple relics in a satchel stitched with the royal sun.

mosk-37b202f43630.speaker: mosk
mosk-37b202f43630.text: The Grotto swallowed it. Sunk in the water, but dry inside, by some blessing.

ketter-d1ba4bd7c9b8.speaker: ketter
ketter-d1ba4bd7c9b8.text: Dwarven smiths sit in chains at the Ashforge. Dobbin swears they will fight for you.

brogan-71eb4e677396.speaker: brogan
brogan-71eb4e677396.text: Smash the chains. Do not pick the locks.

ketter-5006d93a7394.speaker: ketter
ketter-5006d93a7394.text: First floor, the Warrens. Skarn rides a spider, and spiders burn. Bring fire.

brogan-3476c5514866.speaker: brogan
brogan-3476c5514866.text: Rats come in packs. Fight in the corridor, not the open room.

ketter-abad5446ce34.speaker: ketter
ketter-abad5446ce34.text: Old Clubtail hits like a falling roof. Keep your healer behind the line and topped up.

mosk-b07d15443e57.speaker: mosk
mosk-b07d15443e57.text: No healer in your party? Down in the Grotto? Old Clubtail breaks bones.

brogan-a687d6325171.speaker: brogan
brogan-a687d6325171.text: Hire a priest at the bar before you go. It is cheaper than a funeral.

ketter-408f93f2e50d.speaker: ketter
ketter-408f93f2e50d.text: Glasshide the Basilisk turns folk to glass. Thunder shatters it. Poison does nothing.

brogan-60bfef1b7952.speaker: brogan
brogan-60bfef1b7952.text: Gargoyles in the Glimmerdeep shrug off lightning and poison. Hit them with steel.

ketter-4706dcbce08c.speaker: ketter
ketter-4706dcbce08c.text: Forgemaster Brakk shrugs off fire. Odd, for a man who lives in a forge.

mosk-32b0dac2417c.speaker: mosk
mosk-32b0dac2417c.text: The chimera Cindermaw burns, flies and bites three ways. Cold drops it like a stone.

ketter-7c0c23fa70aa.speaker: ketter
ketter-7c0c23fa70aa.text: Malthrax fears radiant light and shrugs off the dark. Bring something that shines.

iolen-46b1bad59ff6.speaker: iolen
iolen-46b1bad59ff6.text: The Sovereign's staff has a crack under the third ring. Find the tall tale and strike there.

brogan-d8210bfed4b9.speaker: brogan
brogan-d8210bfed4b9.text: Another round! And a dwarf's blessing on whoever pays!

mosk-4e3759aa7812.speaker: mosk
mosk-4e3759aa7812.text: Ninety gold, three pelts and a lamp. That is all I have left, and I was robbed twice.

ketter-890730f36245.speaker: ketter
ketter-890730f36245.text: Thirty years in the dungeons. My knees remember every one of them.

iolen-ff99021f427f.speaker: iolen
iolen-ff99021f427f.text: The road is long, but this tavern is warm. I rest here between pilgrimages.

tilda-84adee4cdc87.speaker: tilda
tilda-84adee4cdc87.text: Marga waters the ale. Do not tell her I said so.

brogan-33fec4de56eb.speaker: brogan
brogan-33fec4de56eb.text: I could not tell. Is that bad?

brogan-a47044fb2e9a.speaker: brogan
brogan-a47044fb2e9a.text: I heard the stew has rat in it.

brambur-3bfc297a2427.speaker: brambur
brambur-3bfc297a2427.text: My mum was a smith before she was anything else. She forged a hammer for every child she blessed.

brambur-95795a25df84.speaker: brambur
brambur-95795a25df84.text: Someone took hers from the forge. It is somewhere below us, and I keep apologizing to the rats in case they have it.

brambur-dcb9ebb2556e.speaker: brambur
brambur-dcb9ebb2556e.text: If you see dwarven boot prints, will you tell me? Please? Sorry. Please.

brambur-24184eba63bb.speaker: brambur
brambur-24184eba63bb.text: I did not tell you about my father. He went down a mine and counted the dark instead of the days.

brambur-9ee349d2e2ab.speaker: brambur
brambur-9ee349d2e2ab.text: Mother Pellwen says every second chance is a door. I only have to knock, instead of apologizing to it.

brambur-9b6c336c389c.speaker: brambur
brambur-9b6c336c389c.text: I used to pray for the courage to be brave. Lately I pray for the courage to be useful.

brambur-e4bea7fac98f.speaker: brambur
brambur-e4bea7fac98f.text: You make me useful. I wanted you to know that. It is the nicest thing anyone has done for me.

brambur-2ef50b1a1f3c.speaker: brambur
brambur-2ef50b1a1f3c.text: The hammer has a name. Hearthsong. My mum sang to the iron while she worked.

brambur-251238f423b7.speaker: brambur
brambur-251238f423b7.text: When we find it, I would like you to hear it ring. That is all. That is everything.

fizzwick-06546a7af701.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-06546a7af701.text: Fizzwick's spellbook was scattered by cultists. Pages, you understand, written in his own tiny hand.

fizzwick-4baf1d3627b6.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-4baf1d3627b6.text: Without them Fizzwick is merely brilliant. With them, Fizzwick is inevitable.

fizzwick-83f3f6d119ae.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-83f3f6d119ae.text: Keep an eye out for torn pages. Fizzwick will pretend he does not care.

fizzwick-6532fd836869.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-6532fd836869.text: Fizzwick was expelled from the Academy of Brightspire. Officially, for a fireball in the library.

fizzwick-6d9c6550e4b2.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-6d9c6550e4b2.text: The fireball was peer review, a rather harsh one. The library has since been rebuilt, and it is bigger.

fizzwick-35c7c72dc7cd.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-35c7c72dc7cd.text: Fizzwick will tell you something he has told no one. He fears nobody remembers a gnome who is not loud.

fizzwick-d7b452e5f700.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-d7b452e5f700.text: So Fizzwick is very loud. Even in the dark. Especially in the dark.

fizzwick-c8bd1509c629.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-c8bd1509c629.text: Fizzwick has never had a friend who stayed after the explosion. You stayed.

fizzwick-d050a4431401.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-d050a4431401.text: Fizzwick has noted this in a footnote. It is the longest footnote he has ever written.

pip-8b275e3ff2d0.speaker: pip
pip-8b275e3ff2d0.text: The Lantern Row Crew had eleven. We lit one lantern for each of us, over the old bakery door.

pip-54b6a329e1af.speaker: pip
pip-54b6a329e1af.text: Garrick Vane was my partner, and my best friend. He sold the whole crew to the cult for a pocket of gold.

pip-0636ea81252a.speaker: pip
pip-0636ea81252a.text: So I follow the Lantern Row marks down the floors. Three clues, then the Seneschal's door.

pip-1ff0207d58c1.speaker: pip
pip-1ff0207d58c1.text: Posy was the youngest. Nine years old, pockets like a magician. Garrick swore he would keep her safe.

pip-fab114464a60.speaker: pip
pip-fab114464a60.text: I do not want to talk about Posy. Thank you for not making me.

pip-4d21bbda69fe.speaker: pip
pip-4d21bbda69fe.text: Some nights I plan to stab him. Some nights I plan to hear him say sorry.

pip-2cd4f58413f1.speaker: pip
pip-2cd4f58413f1.text: I like the second plan less. Whatever you decide when we get there, I will remember it. I remember everything.

pip-a2c01d0b78c0.speaker: pip
pip-a2c01d0b78c0.text: I do not trust anybody. But I trust you a little. For me, that is a lot.

pip-e70f163bb153.speaker: pip
pip-e70f163bb153.text: When we reach the Seneschal's door, stand where I can see you. That is all I ask.

grumsh-3e1c01e64f20.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-3e1c01e64f20.text: I am writing a ballad. One verse for every floor of the Blackspire. Five verses, no chorus.

grumsh-50ac5b09e27b.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-50ac5b09e27b.text: My mother wanted a bard. I am a disappointment with a very good rhyme for slaughter.

grumsh-676ab6cbe330.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-676ab6cbe330.text: If you find a verse on a wall, in a carving or a drunk's scrawl, tell me. It may be the one.

grumsh-5965a8690bf4.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-5965a8690bf4.text: My father was a warlord. He taught me to count enemies. My mother taught me to count syllables.

grumsh-1a06091aa059.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-1a06091aa059.text: I am better at the second. No one has ever cheered a syllable.

grumsh-ba7df98adc17.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-ba7df98adc17.text: When I was small, I sang to the wounded in the camp. They said I sounded like a kind storm.

grumsh-b230c09f6a6b.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-b230c09f6a6b.text: Then my father heard. He called it weakness, and I put the songs away for twenty years.

grumsh-dc7a41bf0c2e.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-dc7a41bf0c2e.text: Last night I hummed in my sleep. Brambur says it was lovely.

grumsh-975bfe0684c2.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-975bfe0684c2.text: I will sing the ballad aloud when we win. You may stand at the back. I will still see you.

zizzy-5779a49ac17e.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-5779a49ac17e.text: Zizzy needs blasting powder! Dwarven blasting powder, the good stuff, in the Ashforge somewhere!

zizzy-c42763835226.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-c42763835226.text: The Ashforge gate is locked. Locks are just very small walls, and walls are very slow explosions.

zizzy-b36ba6ca6541.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-b36ba6ca6541.text: Find the powder and Zizzy will make you a firework. A tiny one. Medium.

zizzy-d3b34e30a10b.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-d3b34e30a10b.text: My family did not like the fire. The tiefling parts of me that go boom. They told me to hide it.

zizzy-1aa6358c5c54.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-1aa6358c5c54.text: Zizzy did not hide it. Zizzy made it a hobby, then a career. Look how well it is going!

zizzy-beead22ef13a.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-beead22ef13a.text: Zizzy has a secret. When it is quiet, I get scared the fire will not stop.

zizzy-f6c23d7a56d7.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-f6c23d7a56d7.text: When you are near, it stays small. I do not know why. I am not complaining. Do not tell Vexrath, he will file it.

zizzy-3343c3902758.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-3343c3902758.text: Zizzy made you a gift. A very small firework, shaped like a heart. It exploded. Sorry!

zizzy-b3d1bf3a7b21.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-b3d1bf3a7b21.text: I will make another. You are my favorite explosion and my favorite person, in that order.

vexrath-6d5d412ebe93.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-6d5d412ebe93.text: My clan was exiled by royal decree, forty years ago. I have read the decree. I believe it is forged.

vexrath-fe761ea8ede7.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-fe761ea8ede7.text: The original is sealed in crystal somewhere on the third floor. I will find it, or I will file a complaint.

vexrath-fe14de1b012d.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-fe14de1b012d.text: If you see a royal seal, bring it to me. Bring it gently. It is evidence.

vexrath-78d540482240.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-78d540482240.text: Ledgerus teaches that every promise is a debt, and every debt will be called. I take that seriously.

vexrath-6bba4e1ff438.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-6bba4e1ff438.text: I fear I have not always kept my promises to my own family.

vexrath-36ee88d4596b.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-36ee88d4596b.text: My sister begged me not to sign the exile. I signed. I thought it was the law. It was a lie.

vexrath-a5026f06c1f8.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-a5026f06c1f8.text: I have been filing that mistake in my heart for forty years. It has no folder.

vexrath-8467745c99ff.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-8467745c99ff.text: I have drafted a document. It is a character reference. It is for you.

vexrath-945d968468bb.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-945d968468bb.text: It reads, in full: honest, brave, irregular. Please note that I have stamped it twice.

nettle-51b938de46e5.speaker: nettle
nettle-51b938de46e5.text: I am collecting the true legend of the Sovereign's staff. One fragment per floor, from the second floor down.

nettle-9a5e51bb065d.speaker: nettle
nettle-9a5e51bb065d.text: Everyone agrees on the staff. Nobody agrees on the details. That is how you know it is true.

nettle-205293f62d06.speaker: nettle
nettle-205293f62d06.text: If a smith or a ghost starts talking, listen. I pay in stories.

nettle-af94a06030b2.speaker: nettle
nettle-af94a06030b2.text: Truth time. I did not invent the door. I only wanted to be the sort of person who might have.

nettle-4d99d7179769.speaker: nettle
nettle-4d99d7179769.text: Everything else I told you is true. Possibly. That is the truth.

nettle-dc3b6c58a823.speaker: nettle
nettle-dc3b6c58a823.text: I grew up in a ship's galley. My mother sold stories to sailors for an extra ladle of soup.

nettle-1991e16231c7.speaker: nettle
nettle-1991e16231c7.text: She said a lie is a gift when you give it away. I have given away a great many gifts.

nettle-9c95d136ad2e.speaker: nettle
nettle-9c95d136ad2e.text: I tried writing the true story of this party. It came out better than any lie I own.

nettle-28460b1ea10c.speaker: nettle
nettle-28460b1ea10c.text: I am keeping it. Somebody should remember us properly, and it might as well be a liar.

brambur-c1341bb3a6c5.speaker: brambur
brambur-c1341bb3a6c5.text: Any word of dwarven boot prints? Mum's hammer is out there, on the first floor, and the fourth.

fizzwick-1a8fef4d2ff2.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-1a8fef4d2ff2.text: Fizzwick's missing pages are on the second floor and the third. Torn, in tiny handwriting. You cannot miss them.

pip-540ad3f1cad2.speaker: pip
pip-540ad3f1cad2.text: The Lantern Row marks are on every floor. Three clues, then the Seneschal's door.

grumsh-02466aa32b16.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-02466aa32b16.text: There is a verse waiting on every floor. Wall carvings, drunken scrawls. I will know it when I hear it.

zizzy-4fa18d4d96c4.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-4fa18d4d96c4.text: Blasting powder, in the Ashforge! A keg, a barrel! Zizzy would settle for a thimble.

vexrath-dcb0ed5ff463.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-dcb0ed5ff463.text: The original decree is sealed in crystal on the third floor. I would know the seal anywhere.

nettle-b53a2ee68163.speaker: nettle
nettle-b53a2ee68163.text: One tale fragment per floor, from the second down. Ask the smiths and the ghosts. They love a story.

pip-4ae67c799bb4.speaker: pip
pip-4ae67c799bb4.text: Traps on this floor like dull corridors. Walk slowly, listen for clicks, and check the plate stones.

zizzy-1fd56c51d106.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-1fd56c51d106.text: The spiders on this floor burn! Zizzy will bring the fire. The rats burn too, but they do not enjoy it.

brambur-4392d6e30c26.speaker: brambur
brambur-4392d6e30c26.text: Old Clubtail hits very hard. Keep us healed, and keep the healer standing. That is me. Sorry.

liora-578faa05247c.speaker: liora
liora-578faa05247c.text: The Grotto floods in places. Look for the chapel and the black pool, and listen for singing.

fizzwick-e808b20a3720.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-e808b20a3720.text: Wasps and water. Fizzwick advises thunder, or at least dry socks.

vexrath-33f69342040f.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-33f69342040f.text: Glasshide turns the careless to glass. Thunder shatters it. Poison does nothing. I have filed this.

nettle-0cccb19b3d34.speaker: nettle
nettle-0cccb19b3d34.text: The orchard in the Glimmerdeep is real, and so is the kiln. Look for open sky and a glint of silver.

pip-0998379c114e.speaker: pip
pip-0998379c114e.text: The mirrors on this floor lie. Do not stare at one longer than a breath.

zizzy-71f80810f19a.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-71f80810f19a.text: Cindermaw hates cold! Zizzy has no cold. Zizzy has other fun things.

grumsh-9e1b19b1a71a.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-9e1b19b1a71a.text: Brakk wears fire like a coat. Steel or cold, not flame. I will write him a short verse.

fizzwick-c0717e4d672d.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-c0717e4d672d.text: Smiths in chains. Fizzwick does not enjoy chains. Free them, and they will help us.

liora-df6da57615b6.speaker: liora
liora-df6da57615b6.text: Malthrax hates radiant light, and the dark does nothing. If you have anything holy, save it for him.

nettle-3dc27f9f9df4.speaker: nettle
nettle-3dc27f9f9df4.text: The staff has a crack under the third ring. Strike there and it ends. I have it on good authority.

pip-da0c0a789589.speaker: pip
pip-da0c0a789589.text: The Seneschal's door is somewhere on this floor. Check every wall before you check every door.

brambur-1fd783201157.speaker: brambur
brambur-1fd783201157.text: Rest before you push on, please. A tired party is a sorry party. I am saying sorry in advance.

fizzwick-8866ba86835e.speaker: fizzwick
fizzwick-8866ba86835e.text: Fizzwick advises you to read the walls. Walls are the oldest books, and the rudest.

pip-f0f94e23d2fd.speaker: pip
pip-f0f94e23d2fd.text: Check every chest twice and every door once. Then check your own pockets.

grumsh-33e05432168d.speaker: grumsh
grumsh-33e05432168d.text: Fight with your back to a wall. Make the enemy walk around your rhyme.

zizzy-e8b093421484.speaker: zizzy
zizzy-e8b093421484.text: If it is stuck, burn it. If it is not stuck, ask first. Mostly burn.

vexrath-b320c82b20d8.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-b320c82b20d8.text: Prepare, then proceed. A properly prepared slate of spells wins more fights than courage.

nettle-7ce048737434.speaker: nettle
nettle-7ce048737434.text: When in doubt, ask the ghosts. They love to talk, and they never charge.

liora-6bc95d5b9163.speaker: liora
liora-6bc95d5b9163.text: Watch for loose stones, cold drafts and fresh footprints. The floor always tells the truth.
